## Timeline : Beyoncé

Page **1**

1[2](https://calendar.songfacts.com/timeline/beyonce/page-2)[](https://calendar.songfacts.com/timeline/beyonce/page-2)

September 4, 1981
[Beyoncé Knowles](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) is born in Houston, Texas. She finds fame as the lead singer of the '90s girl group [Destiny's Child](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/destinys-child) before becoming Queen Bey.

March 16, 2000
[Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) and [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) meet for the first time at MTV's Spring Break festival in Cancun, where both are performing (Bey with her group, [Destiny's Child](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/destinys-child)). They go on their first date two years later.

July 26, 2002
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) makes her film debut, playing Mike Myers' love interest, Foxxy Cleopatra, in _Austin Powers in Goldmember_. Her catch phrase: "I'm a whole lotta woman." [Britney Spears](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/britney-spears) also shows up in the film as a fem-bot who gets blown up by Myers.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/july/26/18370)

October 10, 2002
[Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) releases "['03 Bonnie And Clyde](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/jay-z/03-bonnie-and-clyde)," featuring [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) in her first solo appearance since the breakup of [Destiny's Child](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/destinys-child). It's the first hint the couple are dating, as Jay declares them "the new [Bobby](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/bobby-brown) and [Whitney](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/whitney-houston)" on the track.

June 24, 2003
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) releases her first solo album, **Dangerously in Love**. The standout track is "[Crazy In Love](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/crazy-in-love)," which features her boyfriend [Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z).

January 26, 2004
[Britney Spears](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/britney-spears), [Pink](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/pnk) and [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) star as Roman gladiators sent to fight to the death by emperor [Enrique Iglesias](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/enrique-iglesias) in a [lavish Pepsi commercial](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W7jkygJ_QNo). Instead of fighting, they sing "[We Will Rock You](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/queen/we-will-rock-you)" and drink soda.

August 29, 2004
"[Hey Ya!](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/outkast/hey-ya)" wins Video of the Year at the MTV Video Music Awards, one of four wins for [Outkast](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/outkast) on the night. The show also marks the first red carpet appearance for [Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) and [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) as a couple.

February 12, 2006
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) becomes the first woman to star in a #1 movie while having a #1 hit at the same time when _The Pink Panther_ tops the box office as "Check On It" (used in the end credits) remains at the top of the chart. She's the third person to do it, following Prince with _Purple Rain_ and "[When Doves Cry](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/prince/when-doves-cry)," and Eminem with _8 Mile_ and "[Lose Yourself](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/eminem/lose-yourself)."

December 25, 2006
[![Image 2: Jennifer Hudson Makes Acting Debut In Dreamgirls](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-17494.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/december/25/17494)Alongside stars like [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce), [Eddie Murphy](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/eddie-murphy), and [Jamie Foxx](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jamie-foxx), [Jennifer Hudson](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jennifer-hudson) makes her acting debut in the movie _Dreamgirls_, based on the [Supremes](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/the-supremes)-inspired Broadway musical.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/december/25/17494)

April 7, 2007
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce)'s "[Beautiful Liar](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/beautiful-liar)," featuring Latin-pop star [Shakira](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/shakira), breaks the record for the highest leap on the Billboard Hot 100 when it jumps 91 places to #3. The record was previously held by [Akon](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/akon), whose "[Smack That](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/akon/smack-that)," featuring [Eminem](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/eminem), rose from #95 to #7 (ultimately peaking at #2) in 2006.

December 16, 2007
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) hits #1 in America with the [Ne-Yo](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/ne-yo)-penned single "[Irreplaceable](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/irreplaceable)," which spends an astonishing 10 weeks at the top spot.

April 4, 2008
After years of quiet courtship, [Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) and [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) get married in a secret ceremony, becoming the most powerful couple in entertainment.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/april/4/17625)

October 13, 2008
Five months after marrying [Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z), [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) releases the sassy "[Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/single-ladies-put-a-ring-on-it)." It goes to #1 in America for four weeks and win the Grammy for Song of the Year.

December 5, 2008
[![Image 3: Beyonce Channels Etta James In Cadillac Records](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-17482.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/december/5/17482)The musical biopic _Cadillac Records_ premieres in US theaters, with [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) in a starring role as soul legend [Etta James](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/etta-james).[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/december/5/17482)

January 20, 2009
[![Image 4: Beyonce Sings "At Last" For Obamas, Angers Etta James](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-17483.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/january/20/17483)[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) serenades Barack Obama and his wife, Michelle, at the Neighborhood Ball as the couple shares their first dance together as president and first lady of the United States. The choice of song, Etta James' signature hit "[At Last](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/etta-james/at-last)," throws the blues singer into a fit of rage aimed at Beyoncé.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/january/20/17483)

January 18, 2009
A wide range of top musicians including [Mary J. Blige](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/mary-j-blige), [U2](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/u2), [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce), [Bruce Springsteen](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/bruce-springsteen), [Garth Brooks](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/garth-brooks), [Sheryl Crow](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/sheryl-crow), [will.i.am](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/william), [James Taylor](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/james-taylor), [John Legend](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/john-legend), [John Mellencamp](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/john-mellencamp), [Pete Seeger](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/pete-seeger), [Shakira](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/shakira), [Usher](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/usher) and [Stevie Wonder](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/stevie-wonder), perform at a concert in Washington, DC, to celebrate the upcoming inauguration of Barack Obama as President of the United States of America.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/january/18/1818)

September 13, 2009
[![Image 5: Taylor Swift Wins MTV Video Music Award, Kanye West Loses It](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-16175.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/september/13/16175)When [Taylor Swift](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/taylor-swift) wins for Best Female Video at the MTV Video Music Awards, [Kanye West](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/kanye-west) comes on stage and commandeers the microphone, explaining that Beyoncé deserved the award for her "[Single Ladies](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/single-ladies-put-a-ring-on-it)" video. When Beyoncé does win for Video of the Year later that night, she brings Taylor on stage to finish her speech.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/september/13/16175)

January 31, 2010
[![Image 6: Beyonce, Taylor Swift Break Grammy Award Records](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-17471.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/january/31/17471)[Taylor Swift](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/taylor-swift) and [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) sweep the Grammy Awards with record-breaking wins. Earning Album of the Year for **Fearless** at age 19, Swift is the youngest artist to ever win the award. Beyoncé wins six out of ten nominations - including Song of the Year for "[Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/single-ladies-put-a-ring-on-it) " - giving her the most wins in one night of any female artist.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/january/31/17471)

August 28, 2011
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) reveals her pregnancy during the MTV Video Music Awards, setting Twitter on fire.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/august/28/15520)

January 7, 2012
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) and [Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) have their first child: a daughter named Blue Ivy Carter.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/january/7/15828)

August 6, 2012
Forbes declares [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) and [Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) the highest-paid celebrity couple, with earnings of $78 million ($40 million for her, $38 for him). At #2 is Gisele Bundchen and Tom Brady with $72 million.

February 3, 2013
Beyoncé invigorates the 2013 Super Bowl halftime show with a performance that reunites [Destiny's Child](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/destinys-child).[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/february/3/16417)

December 13, 2013
[![Image 7: Beyoncé Drops Surprise Album](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-15715.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/december/13/15715)In a bold and brilliant marketing move, [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce)'s self-titled album is released with no advance notice, sending radio stations scrambling to get the songs on the air and generating lots of free publicity.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/december/13/15715)

June 25, 2014
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) and [Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) kick off their _On The Run_ tour with a show in Miami, with the couple co-headlining. The tour is one of the most profitable ever on a per-show basis, averaging over $5 million per concert.

May 14, 2016
[![Image 8: Every Song From Lemonade Makes The Hot 100](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-17638.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/may/14/17638)Following the release of [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce)'s **Lemonade**, all 12 tracks on the album debut on the Hot 100, breaking [Taylor Swift](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/taylor-swift)'s 2010 record for most songs on the chart at the same time by a female artist.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/may/14/17638)

August 28, 2016
[![Image 9: Beyonce And Rihanna Have VMA Moments](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-17951.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/august/28/17951)At the MTV Video Music Awards, [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) wins Video of the Year for "[Formation](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/formation)." In support of the Black Lives Matter movement, she brings four mothers of shooting victims with her onto the red carpet. By the end of the evening, Bey (along with her production designer, choreographer, director, cinematographer and editor) has eight trophies.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/august/28/17951)

November 2, 2016
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) goes country, performing her song "[Daddy Lessons](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/daddy-lessons)" with the [Dixie Chicks](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/dixie-chicks) at the CMA Awards. Eight years later, she becomes the first Black woman to top the Country chart when "[Texas Hold 'Em](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/texas-hold-em)" goes to #1.

February 1, 2017
In a [post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/BP-rXUGBPJa/) that is liked over 8 million times in 24 hours, [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) reveals she is pregnant with twins.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/february/1/18435)

June 13, 2017
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) and her husband [Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) welcome twins, a girl named Rumi and a boy named Sir.

June 16, 2018
The Carters ([Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) and [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce)) release their first single, "[Apes--t](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/the-carters/apes-t)," with an opulent video shot at the Louvre in Paris.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/june/16/19573)

#### Lauryn Hill Artistfacts

*   May 26, 1975  
*   Lauryn Hill was born in East Orange, New Jersey, but her family would eventually settle in South Orange, where she would meet a fellow future star: actor Zach Braff. 
*   Hill immersed herself in Motown and R&B at a young age when she discovered her mom's old albums in her attic. She began singing in earnest at age 7 when her mom took her to see a production of _Annie_. After that, she drove her family crazy by singing the show's tunes non-stop. 
*   At age 12, Hill competed on the amateur portion of _It's Showtime at the Apollo_, singing the Miracles' "Who's Lovin' You." 
*   Hill met her Fugees bandmates, Prakazrel Michel and his cousin Wyclef Jean, when she was just 13.  
*   Moviegoers may remember Hill from her role in _Sister Act II: Back in the Habit_, but she also had a stint on the CBS soap opera _As the World Turns_ (playing Kira Johnson) and played a gum-chewing elevator operator in the period drama _King of the Hill_, starring Jesse Bradford and Adrien Brody. 
*   Hill wrote much of the material for her debut album, **The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill**, while pregnant with her first child, Zion David, with Rohan Marley (Bob Marley's son). She credits the pregnancy for re-igniting her creativity: "I had the desire to write in a capacity that I hadn't done in a while. I don't know if it's a hormonal or emotional thing... I was very in touch with my feelings at the time." She added: "Every time I got hurt, every time I was disappointed, every time I learned, I just wrote a song." 
*   Hill made the 1999 Grammy Awards a night of firsts. With her five Grammy wins for her debut album: Best New Artist, Best R&B Song, Best Female R&B Vocal Performance, Best R&B Album and Album of the Year - she became the first woman to win five Grammy Awards in the same night, beating Carole's King's record of four. She was also the first woman to earn ten nominations in one year, and the album was the first hip-hop record to win Album of the Year. 
*   Years before stardom came knocking, Hill featured in MC Lyte's 1991 Off-Broadway hip-hop rendering of Shakespeare's _Twelfth Night_. She also appeared that same year as an extra in [the video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hSTzr2V4KMw) for the female rapper's "Poor Georgie." 
*   The Recording Industry Association of America announced on February 16, 2021 that **The Miseducation Of Lauryn Hill** had gone Diamond after selling over 10 million copies in the US. This meant Lauryn Hill made history as the first female rapper to achieve the feat. 
*   A Fugees reunion planned for 2021 was scuttled, but in 2023 the group toured in support of Hill on her The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill 25th Anniversary Tour. At those shows, Fugees would play some song from their catalog along with some Wyclef Jean and Pras solo tracks, then Hill would take the stage for her solo set.

Bob Marley's backup singers, The I Threes, claim they are the "Three Little Birds" in his famous song.

#### [Brand New Book](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/train/brand-new-book)Train

Train wrote the 2011 song "Brand New Book" for the TV show The Biggest Loser - part of the song was used in the opening credits.

[![Image 7: Simple Minds](https://www.songfacts.com/img-artalbums-240-8996ecc1ba0cb184d8471131a249f619.png)](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/simple-minds/dont-you-forget-about-me)
#### [Don't You (Forget About Me)](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/simple-minds/dont-you-forget-about-me)Simple Minds

The prom scene in Pretty in Pink was shot to "Don't You (Forget About Me)," but "If You Leave" was used in the film. That's why the dancers are out of time with the music.

[![Image 8: Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/img-artalbums-240-07d8cef6ce741acbb7bd130a4b7fb735.png)](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/jay-z/hard-knock-life-ghetto-anthem)
#### [Hard Knock Life (Ghetto Anthem)](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/jay-z/hard-knock-life-ghetto-anthem)Jay-Z

Jay-Z's "Hard Knock Life (Ghetto Anthem)" is based on the song "It's A Hard Knock Life" from the Broadway play Annie.

[![Image 9: Steppenwolf](https://www.songfacts.com/img-artalbums-240-f93e633eeaddbefece438270270d3eeb.png)](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/steppenwolf/born-to-be-wild)
#### [Born To Be Wild](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/steppenwolf/born-to-be-wild)Steppenwolf

The first popular song to use the phrase "Heavy Metal" was "Born To Be Wild" by Steppenwolf, which was featured in the movie Easy Rider.

[![Image 10: David Guetta](https://www.songfacts.com/img-artalbums-240-6582cf93d8a1d4efdffa7f7357b8124f.png)](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/david-guetta/titanium)
#### [Titanium](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/david-guetta/titanium)David Guetta

Sia Furler wrote "Titanium" and wanted to give the tune to Katy Perry. She turned it down, so David Guetta recorded it instead using Sia's original demo guide vocal. It became a big hit, especially in the UK, where it went to #1.

## Timeline : Beyoncé

Page **1**

1[2](https://calendar.songfacts.com/timeline/beyonce/page-2)[](https://calendar.songfacts.com/timeline/beyonce/page-2)

September 4, 1981
[Beyoncé Knowles](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) is born in Houston, Texas. She finds fame as the lead singer of the '90s girl group [Destiny's Child](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/destinys-child) before becoming Queen Bey.

March 16, 2000
[Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) and [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) meet for the first time at MTV's Spring Break festival in Cancun, where both are performing (Bey with her group, [Destiny's Child](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/destinys-child)). They go on their first date two years later.

July 26, 2002
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) makes her film debut, playing Mike Myers' love interest, Foxxy Cleopatra, in _Austin Powers in Goldmember_. Her catch phrase: "I'm a whole lotta woman." [Britney Spears](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/britney-spears) also shows up in the film as a fem-bot who gets blown up by Myers.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/july/26/18370)

October 10, 2002
[Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) releases "['03 Bonnie And Clyde](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/jay-z/03-bonnie-and-clyde)," featuring [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) in her first solo appearance since the breakup of [Destiny's Child](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/destinys-child). It's the first hint the couple are dating, as Jay declares them "the new [Bobby](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/bobby-brown) and [Whitney](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/whitney-houston)" on the track.

June 24, 2003
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) releases her first solo album, **Dangerously in Love**. The standout track is "[Crazy In Love](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/crazy-in-love)," which features her boyfriend [Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z).

January 26, 2004
[Britney Spears](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/britney-spears), [Pink](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/pnk) and [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) star as Roman gladiators sent to fight to the death by emperor [Enrique Iglesias](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/enrique-iglesias) in a [lavish Pepsi commercial](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W7jkygJ_QNo). Instead of fighting, they sing "[We Will Rock You](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/queen/we-will-rock-you)" and drink soda.

August 29, 2004
"[Hey Ya!](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/outkast/hey-ya)" wins Video of the Year at the MTV Video Music Awards, one of four wins for [Outkast](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/outkast) on the night. The show also marks the first red carpet appearance for [Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) and [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) as a couple.

February 12, 2006
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) becomes the first woman to star in a #1 movie while having a #1 hit at the same time when _The Pink Panther_ tops the box office as "Check On It" (used in the end credits) remains at the top of the chart. She's the third person to do it, following Prince with _Purple Rain_ and "[When Doves Cry](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/prince/when-doves-cry)," and Eminem with _8 Mile_ and "[Lose Yourself](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/eminem/lose-yourself)."

December 25, 2006
[![Image 2: Jennifer Hudson Makes Acting Debut In Dreamgirls](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-17494.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/december/25/17494)Alongside stars like [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce), [Eddie Murphy](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/eddie-murphy), and [Jamie Foxx](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jamie-foxx), [Jennifer Hudson](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jennifer-hudson) makes her acting debut in the movie _Dreamgirls_, based on the [Supremes](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/the-supremes)-inspired Broadway musical.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/december/25/17494)

April 7, 2007
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce)'s "[Beautiful Liar](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/beautiful-liar)," featuring Latin-pop star [Shakira](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/shakira), breaks the record for the highest leap on the Billboard Hot 100 when it jumps 91 places to #3. The record was previously held by [Akon](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/akon), whose "[Smack That](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/akon/smack-that)," featuring [Eminem](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/eminem), rose from #95 to #7 (ultimately peaking at #2) in 2006.

December 16, 2007
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) hits #1 in America with the [Ne-Yo](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/ne-yo)-penned single "[Irreplaceable](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/irreplaceable)," which spends an astonishing 10 weeks at the top spot.

April 4, 2008
After years of quiet courtship, [Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) and [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) get married in a secret ceremony, becoming the most powerful couple in entertainment.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/april/4/17625)

October 13, 2008
Five months after marrying [Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z), [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) releases the sassy "[Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/single-ladies-put-a-ring-on-it)." It goes to #1 in America for four weeks and win the Grammy for Song of the Year.

December 5, 2008
[![Image 3: Beyonce Channels Etta James In Cadillac Records](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-17482.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/december/5/17482)The musical biopic _Cadillac Records_ premieres in US theaters, with [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) in a starring role as soul legend [Etta James](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/etta-james).[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/december/5/17482)

January 20, 2009
[![Image 4: Beyonce Sings "At Last" For Obamas, Angers Etta James](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-17483.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/january/20/17483)[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) serenades Barack Obama and his wife, Michelle, at the Neighborhood Ball as the couple shares their first dance together as president and first lady of the United States. The choice of song, Etta James' signature hit "[At Last](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/etta-james/at-last)," throws the blues singer into a fit of rage aimed at Beyoncé.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/january/20/17483)

January 18, 2009
A wide range of top musicians including [Mary J. Blige](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/mary-j-blige), [U2](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/u2), [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce), [Bruce Springsteen](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/bruce-springsteen), [Garth Brooks](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/garth-brooks), [Sheryl Crow](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/sheryl-crow), [will.i.am](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/william), [James Taylor](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/james-taylor), [John Legend](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/john-legend), [John Mellencamp](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/john-mellencamp), [Pete Seeger](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/pete-seeger), [Shakira](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/shakira), [Usher](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/usher) and [Stevie Wonder](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/stevie-wonder), perform at a concert in Washington, DC, to celebrate the upcoming inauguration of Barack Obama as President of the United States of America.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/january/18/1818)

September 13, 2009
[![Image 5: Taylor Swift Wins MTV Video Music Award, Kanye West Loses It](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-16175.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/september/13/16175)When [Taylor Swift](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/taylor-swift) wins for Best Female Video at the MTV Video Music Awards, [Kanye West](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/kanye-west) comes on stage and commandeers the microphone, explaining that Beyoncé deserved the award for her "[Single Ladies](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/single-ladies-put-a-ring-on-it)" video. When Beyoncé does win for Video of the Year later that night, she brings Taylor on stage to finish her speech.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/september/13/16175)

January 31, 2010
[![Image 6: Beyonce, Taylor Swift Break Grammy Award Records](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-17471.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/january/31/17471)[Taylor Swift](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/taylor-swift) and [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) sweep the Grammy Awards with record-breaking wins. Earning Album of the Year for **Fearless** at age 19, Swift is the youngest artist to ever win the award. Beyoncé wins six out of ten nominations - including Song of the Year for "[Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/single-ladies-put-a-ring-on-it) " - giving her the most wins in one night of any female artist.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/january/31/17471)

August 28, 2011
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) reveals her pregnancy during the MTV Video Music Awards, setting Twitter on fire.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/august/28/15520)

January 7, 2012
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) and [Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) have their first child: a daughter named Blue Ivy Carter.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/january/7/15828)

August 6, 2012
Forbes declares [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) and [Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) the highest-paid celebrity couple, with earnings of $78 million ($40 million for her, $38 for him). At #2 is Gisele Bundchen and Tom Brady with $72 million.

February 3, 2013
Beyoncé invigorates the 2013 Super Bowl halftime show with a performance that reunites [Destiny's Child](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/destinys-child).[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/february/3/16417)

December 13, 2013
[![Image 7: Beyoncé Drops Surprise Album](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-15715.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/december/13/15715)In a bold and brilliant marketing move, [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce)'s self-titled album is released with no advance notice, sending radio stations scrambling to get the songs on the air and generating lots of free publicity.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/december/13/15715)

June 25, 2014
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) and [Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) kick off their _On The Run_ tour with a show in Miami, with the couple co-headlining. The tour is one of the most profitable ever on a per-show basis, averaging over $5 million per concert.

May 14, 2016
[![Image 8: Every Song From Lemonade Makes The Hot 100](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-17638.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/may/14/17638)Following the release of [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce)'s **Lemonade**, all 12 tracks on the album debut on the Hot 100, breaking [Taylor Swift](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/taylor-swift)'s 2010 record for most songs on the chart at the same time by a female artist.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/may/14/17638)

August 28, 2016
[![Image 9: Beyonce And Rihanna Have VMA Moments](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-17951.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/august/28/17951)At the MTV Video Music Awards, [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) wins Video of the Year for "[Formation](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/formation)." In support of the Black Lives Matter movement, she brings four mothers of shooting victims with her onto the red carpet. By the end of the evening, Bey (along with her production designer, choreographer, director, cinematographer and editor) has eight trophies.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/august/28/17951)

November 2, 2016
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) goes country, performing her song "[Daddy Lessons](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/daddy-lessons)" with the [Dixie Chicks](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/dixie-chicks) at the CMA Awards. Eight years later, she becomes the first Black woman to top the Country chart when "[Texas Hold 'Em](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/texas-hold-em)" goes to #1.

February 1, 2017
In a [post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/BP-rXUGBPJa/) that is liked over 8 million times in 24 hours, [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) reveals she is pregnant with twins.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/february/1/18435)

June 13, 2017
[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) and her husband [Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) welcome twins, a girl named Rumi and a boy named Sir.

June 16, 2018
The Carters ([Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) and [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce)) release their first single, "[Apes--t](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/the-carters/apes-t)," with an opulent video shot at the Louvre in Paris.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/june/16/19573)

## Timeline : Brandy

February 11, 1979
[Brandy](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/brandy) (Brandy Norwood) is born in McComb, Mississippi. She's just 15 in 1994 when she lands her first hit, "[I Wanna Be Down](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/brandy/i-wanna-be-down)." In 1998 she teams with Monica for the iconic duet "[The Boy Is Mine](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/brandy-monica/the-boy-is-mine)."

September 7, 1994
Fifteen-year-old [Brandy](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/brandy) releases her self-titled debut album, which goes on to sell over 4 million copies and establish her as an R&B star. Hits from the album include "I Wanna Be Down" and "Baby."

January 23, 1996
The TV series _Moesha_, starring [Brandy](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/brandy) as a high-school student in California, debuts on UPN, where it runs for six seasons.

May 25, 1996
Seventeen-year-old basketball phenom Kobe Bryant takes the singer [Brandy](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/brandy), also 17, to his prom in Philadelphia. The pair met earlier that year at the Essence Awards. They never get romantically involved but remain friends.

November 2, 1997
[Brandy](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/brandy) becomes the first black Disney princess when she plays Cinderella in the ABC TV movie. [Whitney Houston](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/whitney-houston) plays her Fairy Godmother.

June 6, 1998
Powered by a faux feud contrived by their label, "[The Boy Is Mine](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/brandy-monica/the-boy-is-mine)" by Brandy and Monica hits #1, where it stays for 13 weeks, longer than any other female duet. They perform the song together just once (at the 1998 MTV Video Music Awards) until 2012, when they start sharing the stage for showcases and "battles." In 2025 they team up for The Boy Is Mine tour, with the song used as the closer.

September 15, 1998
Brandy and Monica, who have been lighting up the chatrooms on AOL, perform their duet "[The Boy Is Mine](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/brandy-monica/the-boy-is-mine)" at the MTV Video Music Awards amid rumors that the young divas have serious beef. Clearing things up, their managers issue a statement saying: "The fact is that Brandy and Monica did interviews together, had their picture taken together, had adjoining dressing rooms, sat together at the show, and held hands and prayed together prior to going on stage to perform."

May 16, 1999
[Diana Ross](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/diana-ross) and [Brandy](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/brandy) star as mother and daughter in the made-for-TV movie _Double Platinum_.

May 14, 2001
After a six-season run, the last episode of [Brandy](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/brandy)'s TV series _Moesha_ airs. This final episode is a cliffhanger, with Moesha learning she is pregnant and her brother getting kidnapped.

December 30, 2006
R&B superstar [Brandy](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/brandy) is involved in a car accident on the 405 freeway in Los Angeles that kills a 38-year-old woman who is struck by her Land Rover. No criminal charges are files, and a civil suit is later settled.

October 19, 2021
The TV series _Queens_, starring [Brandy](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/brandy) and [Eve](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/eve) as members of a hip-hop group from the '90s who reunite in the '20s, debuts on ABC.

## Music History Events: Awards and Honors

Page **1**

1[2](https://calendar.songfacts.com/category/awards-and-honors/page-2)...[24](https://calendar.songfacts.com/category/awards-and-honors/page-24)[](https://calendar.songfacts.com/category/awards-and-honors/page-2)

[![Image 2: Billie Eilish Wins Big At Grammys](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-20357.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/january/26/20357)January 26, 2020[Billie Eilish](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/billie-eilish), 18, wins big at the Grammys as the death of Kobe Bryant and an internal scandal cast a cloud on the ceremony.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/january/26/20357)

September 10, 2018[John Legend](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/john-legend), Andrew Lloyd Webber and Tim Rice all win Emmys for their work on the NBC special _Jesus Christ Superstar Live in Concert_, earning all three EGOT. Only 12 other people had previously won an Emmy, Grammy, Oscar and Tony. Legend's Oscar came from "[Glory](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/john-legend/glory)"; his Tony for production work on _Jitney_.

November 27, 2017 Country singer [Blake Shelton](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/blake-shelton) is named _People_ magazine's "Sexiest Man Alive." He's the second musician to receive the honor in the annual feature's 32-year run; the first was [Adam Levine](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/adam-levine), his fellow coach on _The Voice_, in 2013.

June 15, 2017[Jay-Z](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jay-z) becomes the first rapper inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame.

April 7, 2017[Pearl Jam](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/pearl-jam), Nile Rodgers, [Electric Light Orchestra](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/electric-light-orchestra), [Journey](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/journey), [Joan Baez](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/joan-baez), [Tupac Shakur](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/2pac) and [Yes](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/yes) are inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/april/7/18745)

March 18, 2017[Katy Perry](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/katy-perry) accepts the National Equality Award from the Human Rights Campaign for her work supporting LGBTQ causes. In her speech, she admits that she did more than just [kiss a girl](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/katy-perry/i-kissed-a-girl).[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/march/18/18584)

February 22, 2017 Longtime [blink-182](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/blink-182) frontman Tom DeLonge receives the UFO Researcher Of The Year Award at the International UFO Congress.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/february/22/18522)

[![Image 3: Adele Restarts George Michael Tribute At Grammys](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-18455.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/february/12/18455)February 12, 2017[Adele](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/adele) opens the Grammy Awards with a performance of "[Hello](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/adele/hello)," which wins for Song of the Year and Record of the Year. Later, she sings "[Fastlove](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/george-michael/fastlove)" in a tribute to George Michael, who passed away on Christmas day, 2016. Before she can finish the first chorus, she stops the song and starts over, saying, "I can't mess this up for him."[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/february/12/18455)

February 10, 2017[Tom Petty](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/tom-petty) is honored as Person of the Year at the MusiCares gala, held two days before the Grammy Awards. "Twenty years ago I'd have been way too cynical to do this, but I'm 66 now and I feel ya," he says in his speech.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/february/10/18858)

December 10, 2016[Bob Dylan](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/bob-dylan) accepts the Nobel Prize in Literature. He doesn't attend the ceremony, but sends an insightful speech that is read by the US ambassador to Sweden.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/december/10/18213)

February 28, 2016 At the Oscars, Lady Gaga is introduced by Vice President Joe Biden and performs "[Til It Happens To You](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/lady-gaga/til-it-happens-to-you)" joined by a group of sexual assault survivors. A few minutes later, it loses the Best Song award to Sam Smith's "[Writing's On The Wall](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/sam-smith/writings-on-the-wall)."[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/february/28/17516)

[![Image 4: Taylor Swift Fires Back At The Grammys](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-17492.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/february/15/17492)February 15, 2016 In her Grammy acceptance speech for Album of the Year, [Taylor Swift](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/taylor-swift) warns of "people along the way who will try to undercut your success or take credit for your accomplishments or your fame." This is in response to [Kanye West](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/kanye-west), who rapped about Swift, "I made that bitch famous" in his song "[Famous](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/kanye-west/famous)."[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/february/15/17492)

[![Image 5: Elvis Gets Another Stamp](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-17732.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/august/12/17732)August 12, 2015[Elvis Presley](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/elvis-presley) is granted the honor of a second postage stamp bearing his likeness (the first was introduced in 1993). This one features a black-and-white photograph by William Speer of Elvis in 1955 and is part of the Music Icon series that began in 2013.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/august/12/17732)

March 2, 2014 _20 Feet From Stardom_, a film about backup singers featuring [Darlene Love](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/darlene-love) and Lisa Fischer, wins the Oscar for Best Documentary. Love gets a standing ovation when she sings part of her acceptance speech.

November 19, 2013 _People_ magazine names [Adam Levine](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/adam-levine) "Sexiest Man Alive," making him the first musician to earn the title in the feature's 28-year history.

April 18, 2013[Public Enemy](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/public-enemy) become the fourth hip-hop act inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame (the others that preceded PE into the Hall were [Grandmaster Flash & the Furious Five](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/grandmaster-flash-the-furious-five), [Run-DMC](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/run-dmc), and the [Beastie Boys](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beastie-boys)). Other 2013 inductees are [Rush](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/rush), [Heart](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/heart) (which reunites their original lineup), [Albert King](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/albert-king), [Donna Summer](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/donna-summer), and [Randy Newman](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/randy-newman).

October 16, 2012[Darius Rucker](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/darius-rucker) is inducted into the Grand Ole Opry. He's just the third African American to join the club, following cast member DeFord Bailey and Charley Pride, who was inducted in 1993.

April 14, 2012[Red Hot Chili Peppers](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/red-hot-chili-peppers), [Beastie Boys](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beastie-boys), [Guns N' Roses](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/guns-n-roses) and [Faces](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/faces) are inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/april/14/17435)

August 28, 2011[Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) reveals her pregnancy during the MTV Video Music Awards, setting Twitter on fire.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/august/28/15520)

July 29, 2011[Chuck Berry](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/chuck-berry) throws out the first pitch at the St. Louis Cardinals baseball game on the same day his statue is unveiled on Delmar Boulevard in the city.

March 14, 2011 Long-neglected [Neil Diamond](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/neil-diamond) is finally inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame along with [Alice Cooper](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/alice-cooper), [Tom Waits](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/tom-waits), [Dr. John](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/dr-john), [Darlene Love](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/darlene-love) and [Leon Russell](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/leon-russell).

March 15, 2010 The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame class of 2010 - [ABBA](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/abba), [Jimmy Cliff](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jimmy-cliff), [Genesis](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/genesis), [The Hollies](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/the-hollies), [The Stooges](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/the-stooges) - are inducted at the 25th Annual Rock and Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at the Waldorf-Astoria in New York City.

[![Image 6: Beyonce, Taylor Swift Break Grammy Award Records](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-17471.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/january/31/17471)January 31, 2010[Taylor Swift](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/taylor-swift) and [Beyoncé](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) sweep the Grammy Awards with record-breaking wins. Earning Album of the Year for **Fearless** at age 19, Swift is the youngest artist to ever win the award. Beyoncé wins six out of ten nominations - including Song of the Year for "[Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/single-ladies-put-a-ring-on-it) " - giving her the most wins in one night of any female artist.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/january/31/17471)

[![Image 7: Taylor Swift Wins MTV Video Music Award, Kanye West Loses It](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-16175.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/september/13/16175)September 13, 2009 When [Taylor Swift](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/taylor-swift) wins for Best Female Video at the MTV Video Music Awards, [Kanye West](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/kanye-west) comes on stage and commandeers the microphone, explaining that Beyoncé deserved the award for her "[Single Ladies](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/single-ladies-put-a-ring-on-it)" video. When Beyoncé does win for Video of the Year later that night, she brings Taylor on stage to finish her speech.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/september/13/16175)

[![Image 8: Brit Awards Reach Peak Duffy](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-18831.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/february/18/18831)February 18, 2009[Duffy](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/duffy) is the big winner at the Brit Awards, taking Album of the Year for **Rockferry** along with gongs for British Female Solo Artist and British Breakthrough Act, beating out [Adele](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/adele) in those two categories.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/february/18/18831)

January 11, 2009[Bruce Springsteen](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/bruce-springsteen) wins Best Song from a Motion Picture for "[The Wrestler](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/bruce-springsteen/the-wrestler)" at the Golden Globe Awards. Mickey Rourke wins for Best Actor in a Drama for his work on the film.

November 6, 2008 Thanks to internet voting, [Rick Astley](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/rick-astley) wins Best Act Ever at the MTV Europe Music Awards. "We've been well and truly Rickrolled," the show's producer says.

April 7, 2008[Bob Dylan](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/bob-dylan) gets an honorary Pulitzer Prize for his "profound impact on popular music and American culture." He's the first rock musician to win the award.

[![Image 9: Call Him Dr. May](https://calendar.songfacts.com/img-150-3656.jpg)](https://calendar.songfacts.com/august/23/3656)August 23, 2007 Brian May of [Queen](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/queen) gets a degree from London's Imperial College. It's not one of those honorary degrees either - he earned a PhD in astrophysics. He would have gotten it sooner, but he was busy being a rock star.[More](https://calendar.songfacts.com/august/23/3656)

May 23, 2007 The US Library of Congress hands out the first Gershwin Award to [Paul Simon](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/paul-simon) for being a "performer whose lifetime contributions exemplify the standard of excellence associated with the Gershwins."

## Timeline : Cardi B

October 11, 1992
[Cardi B](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/cardi-b) is born Belcalis Almanzar in Edgewater, New Jersey. After two seasons on the reality show _Love & Hip-Hop_, her music career takes off with the 2017 #1 hit "[Bodak Yellow](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/cardi-b/bodak-yellow)." Over the next few years, she establishes herself as an uninhibited fashion icon and top rapper.

December 14, 2015
[Cardi B](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/cardi-b), known on social media for pithy posts about her time as an exotic dancer, makes her debut on the reality show _Love & Hip Hop: New York_, where she stars for two seasons. She releases her first single two years later, the #1 hit "[Bodak Yellow](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/cardi-b/bodak-yellow)."

June 16, 2017
[Cardi B](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/cardi-b) releases her debut single, "[Bodak Yellow](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/cardi-b/bodak-yellow)." The title is a nod to the rapper Kodak Black, whose flow she borrows on the track. The song elevates her from social media/reality TV star to renown rapper when the song climbs to #1.

September 20, 2017
[Cardi B](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/cardi-b) and Migos rapper Offset get married at home, wearing sweatpants, in a secret ceremony. He formally proposes to her a month later during her performance in Philadelphia, presenting her with an eight-carat diamond ring. They have their first child, daughter Kulture, the following year.

October 7, 2017
[Cardi B](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/cardi-b) hits #1 in the US with "[Bodak Yellow](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/cardi-b/bodak-yellow)," becoming the first solo female rapper without a guest artist to reach the top since Lauryn Hill's "[Doo Wop (That Thing)](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/lauryn-hill/doo-wop-that-thing)" in 1998.

April 7, 2018
[Cardi B](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/cardi-b) makes her debut as musical guest on _Saturday Night Live_, where she shows off her baby bump to reveal that she's pregnant. She gives birth to daughter Kulture three months later.

April 6, 2018
[Cardi B](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/cardi-b) releases her debut album, **Invasion Of Privacy**. It goes to #1 and clears a path for female rappers like [Megan Thee Stallion](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/megan-thee-stallion) and GloRilla.

July 10, 2018
[Cardi B](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/cardi-b) and Offset have their first child together, a daughter named Kulture. Two weeks later, Cardi pulls out of a planned tour with Bruno Mars so she can spend more time with her.

July 7, 2018
[Cardi B](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/cardi-b) lands her second #1 hit (following "[Bodak Yellow](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/cardi-b/bodak-yellow)") with "[I Like It](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/cardi-b/i-like-it)," a team-up with Bad Bunny and J Balvin. It's the first in a string of hit collaborations for Cardi that includes "[Girls Like You](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/maroon-5/girls-like-you)" with Maroon 5 and "[WAP](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/cardi-b/wap)" with Megan Thee Stallion.

September 7, 2018
Simmering tensions between [Cardi B](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/cardi-b) and [Nicki Minaj](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/nicki-minaj) boil over at a New York Fashion Week party when the pair scuffle and Cardi throws a shoe at Minaj. They settle into a longstanding feud, repeatedly taking shots at each other in lyrics and social media posts.

September 13, 2019
[Lizzo](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/lizzo), [Cardi B](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/cardi-b) and [Jennifer Lopez](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/jennifer-lopez) play strippers in the movie _Hustlers_, which also features [Usher](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/usher) as a patron. It's the film debut for Cardi, who was an exotic dancer before launching her music career.

August 22, 2020
"[WAP](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/cardi-b/wap)" by [Cardi B](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/cardi-b) and [Megan Thee Stallion](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/megan-thee-stallion) hits #1 in America, becoming the most sexually explicit song ever to top the tally. It's bumped off two weeks later by a wholesome slice of K-pop: "[Dynamite](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/bts/dynamite)" by BTS.

January 25, 2022
A jury awards [Cardi B](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/cardi-b) roughly $4 million in her defamation case against YouTube personality Tasha K, who then files bankruptcy. It's a rare case of an artist fighting back against an online critic broadly protected by free speech. Tasha posted dozens of videos alleging drug use, prostitution, infidelity and other misdeeds that were proven false.

December 10, 2023
TikTok stages their first live music event with a five-hour concert in Mesa, Arizona, featuring [Charlie Puth](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/charlie-puth), [Cardi B](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/cardi-b), Peso Pluma and a slate of emerging artists. 17,000 phone-wielding fans attend the sold-out show, with over 9 million more watching online.

September 19, 2025
The album-averse [Cardi B](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/cardi-b) (she usually releases singles) finally drops her second long-player, **Am I the Drama?**. Like her 2018 debut, **Invasion Of Privacy**, it goes to #1, putting her in company of her rival, Nicki Minaj, as the only female rappers to hit the top spot with their first two albums.

#### Lauryn Hill Artistfacts

*   May 26, 1975  
*   Lauryn Hill was born in East Orange, New Jersey, but her family would eventually settle in South Orange, where she would meet a fellow future star: actor Zach Braff. 
*   Hill immersed herself in Motown and R&B at a young age when she discovered her mom's old albums in her attic. She began singing in earnest at age 7 when her mom took her to see a production of _Annie_. After that, she drove her family crazy by singing the show's tunes non-stop. 
*   At age 12, Hill competed on the amateur portion of _It's Showtime at the Apollo_, singing the Miracles' "Who's Lovin' You." 
*   Hill met her Fugees bandmates, Prakazrel Michel and his cousin Wyclef Jean, when she was just 13.  
*   Moviegoers may remember Hill from her role in _Sister Act II: Back in the Habit_, but she also had a stint on the CBS soap opera _As the World Turns_ (playing Kira Johnson) and played a gum-chewing elevator operator in the period drama _King of the Hill_, starring Jesse Bradford and Adrien Brody. 
*   Hill wrote much of the material for her debut album, **The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill**, while pregnant with her first child, Zion David, with Rohan Marley (Bob Marley's son). She credits the pregnancy for re-igniting her creativity: "I had the desire to write in a capacity that I hadn't done in a while. I don't know if it's a hormonal or emotional thing... I was very in touch with my feelings at the time." She added: "Every time I got hurt, every time I was disappointed, every time I learned, I just wrote a song." 
*   Hill made the 1999 Grammy Awards a night of firsts. With her five Grammy wins for her debut album: Best New Artist, Best R&B Song, Best Female R&B Vocal Performance, Best R&B Album and Album of the Year - she became the first woman to win five Grammy Awards in the same night, beating Carole's King's record of four. She was also the first woman to earn ten nominations in one year, and the album was the first hip-hop record to win Album of the Year. 
*   Years before stardom came knocking, Hill featured in MC Lyte's 1991 Off-Broadway hip-hop rendering of Shakespeare's _Twelfth Night_. She also appeared that same year as an extra in [the video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hSTzr2V4KMw) for the female rapper's "Poor Georgie." 
*   The Recording Industry Association of America announced on February 16, 2021 that **The Miseducation Of Lauryn Hill** had gone Diamond after selling over 10 million copies in the US. This meant Lauryn Hill made history as the first female rapper to achieve the feat. 
*   A Fugees reunion planned for 2021 was scuttled, but in 2023 the group toured in support of Hill on her The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill 25th Anniversary Tour. At those shows, Fugees would play some song from their catalog along with some Wyclef Jean and Pras solo tracks, then Hill would take the stage for her solo set.

September 4, 1981[Beyoncé Knowles](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/beyonce) is born in Houston, Texas. She finds fame as the lead singer of the '90s girl group [Destiny's Child](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/destinys-child) before becoming Queen Bey.

June 1, 1981[Brandi Carlile](https://www.songfacts.com/songs/brandi-carlile) is born in the tiny town of Ravensdale, Washington. As her music gets more refined, her audience grows, and by 2019 she's a consistent Grammy winner with a legion of fans.

# Annette Bening

[See the Hollywood Walk of Fame Star Ceremony announcement](http://www.hollywoodchamber.net/newsletter/pr/annette-bening-pr.jpg)  
**Annette Francine Bening** is an American actress. Her break-through role in _The Grifters_ was followed with critically acclaimed roles in films such as _Bugsy_ and _American Beauty_. In 1992, she married American actor and director Warren Beatty, with whom she has four children.

Bening was born in Topeka, Kansas, the daughter of Shirley, a church singer and soloist, and Arnett Grant Bening, a sales training consultant and insurance salesman. Her parents, natives of Iowa, were practicing Episcopalians and conservative Republicans. Her sister and two brothers are Jane Bening, Bradley Bening and Byron Bening. The family moved to Wichita, Kansas, in 1959, where she spent her early childhood. In 1965, her father took a job with a company in San Diego, California, and they moved there. She began acting in junior high school, playing the lead in _The Sound of Music_. She studied drama at Patrick Henry High School.

She then spent a year working as a cook on a charter boat taking fishing parties out on the Pacific Ocean, and scuba diving for recreation. She attended San Diego Mesa College, then completed an academic degree in theatre arts at San Francisco State University. Bening joined the acting company at the American Conservatory Theater in San Francisco while studying acting as part of the Advanced Theatre Training Program. During this time she established herself as a formidable acting talent in roles like Shakespeare’s Lady Macbeth.

Bening moved to New York City, where she debuted off-Broadway at Second Stage Theatre in the role of ‘Holly Dancer’ in Tina Howe’s widely acclaimed _Coastal Disturbances_ opposite Tim Daly, and for which she earned a Tony Award nomination for Best Featured Actress in a Play. However, despite the praise and recognition, it took some time for that success to translate to her film career. Her television debut was with the made-for-TV movie _Manhunt for Claude Dallas_. Her first major role in a theatrical feature was in _The Great Outdoors_ playing ‘Kate Craig’ opposite Dan Aykroyd and John Candy. Her next role was as the Marquise de Merteuil in _Valmont_ opposite Colin Firth.

 #### [1. Kay Panabaker](link_45) 

    *   Actress
    *   Additional Crew
    *   Soundtrack

[Fame (2009)](link_46)

Stephanie Kay Panabaker is an American actress, who was born on May 2, 1990 in Orange Grove, Texas, USA. She is the daughter of Donna (née Mayock) and Harold Panabaker. She has an older sister, [Danielle Panabaker](link_47), who is also an actress. She started acting at various community theaters in Chicago, Philadelphia and Atlanta. In Naperville, Illinois, Kay attended Crone Middle School for sixth grade, and moved to Los Angeles, California, at the start of seventh grade. In between projects, Kay focuses on her academics. She graduated from high school, as valedictorian, when she was thirteen-years-old and received her Associate's Degree at age fifteen. Kay received two academic scholarships from Glendale Community College, where she attended, studying acting, and where she was on the Dean's list, graduating with honors. She was accepted to the UCLA online program as a junior history major, when she was fifteen, and completed her online BA in History from UCLA, before she turned eighteen. Kay was inspired by an elementary school teacher, who made learning exciting, and she wants to do the same for others, hoping to teach 4th or 5th grade, once she finishes her teaching degree. Panabaker has guest-starred in several television dramas and soap operas. She portrayed "Alice Brand" in [7th Heaven (1996)](link_48); "Melissa Rue" in [ER (1994)](link_49); "Sara" in [Port Charles (1997)](link_50); "Carrie Bauer" in [The Brothers Garcia (2000)](link_51); "Elisha" in [Medium (2005)](link_52); "Lindsey Willows" in [CSI: Crime Scene Investigation (2000)](link_53); to name a few. In film, she appeared in [Dead Heat (2002)](link_54) as "Sam LaRoche"; and did some voice work in the Disney/Pixas film, [Monsters, Inc. (2001)](link_55). Panabaker's breakout role came when she starred in The WB's [Summerland (2004)](link_56) as "Nikki Westerly", in the 2004-2005 season. She also appeared as "Georgie" in [Nancy Drew (2007)](link_57), alongside [Emma Roberts](link_58) and [Amy Bruckner](link_59). She starred in the 2007 movie, [Moondance Alexander (2007)](link_60), along with actors, [Don Johnson](link_61), [Lori Loughlin](link_62), [James Best](link_63), [Sasha Cohen](link_64) and [Whitney Sloan](link_65). She co-starred on the ABC sci-fi series, [No Ordinary Family (2010)](link_66), along with actors [Michael Chiklis](link_67), [Julie Benz](link_68), [Jimmy Bennett](link_69), [Autumn Reeser](link_70), [Romany Malco](link_71) and [Stephen Collins](link_72).

 #### [2. Anna Maria Perez de Tagle](link_74)

[Fame (2009)](link_75)

Anna Maria Perez de Tagle was born on December 23, 1990 in San Francisco, California as Anna Maria Francesca Enriquez Perez de Tagle. She's 1 of today's hottest triple threats, w/ an extensive list of accomplishments like acting, singing & dancing. She has opened for the Jonas Brothers Asia tour in 2012 & starred in Godspell on Broadway. She has been featured on shows such as [Late Show with David Letterman (1993)](link_76), [The View (1997)](link_77)&[The Rosie Show (2011)](link_78). She was also featured in a sold-out concert that took place May 7, 2012 on board the Hornblower Hybrid in New York City, benefiting St. Jude Children's Research Hospital.  
  
She was voted Best Featured Female Artist in a Musical at the 2012 Broadway World Awards.  
  
She starred in [Camp Rock (2008)](link_79)&[Camp Rock 2: The Final Jam (2010)](link_80) as Ella, then guest starred in [Baby Daddy (2012)](link_81) as Jenna. She also had a recurring role in [Hannah Montana (2006)](link_82) as Ashley Dewitt.  
  
In 2009, she stole the screen in [Fame (2009)](link_83) as Joy. In 2010, she toured w/ [Demi Lovato](link_84)&[Jonas Brothers](link_85) in North as well as South America. She served as an opener & performer.  
  
At the Ronald Reagan Centennial Birthday Celebration, former 1st lady [Nancy Reagan](link_86) requested her to perform 2 of her favorite Broadway songs in front of hundreds of dignitaries at the Ronald Reagan Library: I Dreamed A Dream from Les Misérables & Someone Like You from Jekyll & Hyde.  
  
She enjoys working w/ the Children's Hospital of L.A., St. Jude's Research Hospital & the American Diabetes Association as well as singing, dancing, working out & reading.  
  
She resides in NYC & L.A.

 #### [3. Sarah Hyland](link_88) 

    *   Actress
    *   Producer
    *   Writer

[Vampire Academy (2014)](link_89)

Sarah Hyland was born in New York City to actors [Melissa D. Canaday](link_90) and [Edward James Hyland](link_91). She began in the business at the age of 4 with commercial work and voice overs. Her first film was [Private Parts (1997)](link_92). She then moved on to [The Object of My Affection (1998)](link_93) and then spent time on [Another World (1964)](link_94) as "Rain Wolfe", a child found in the park, and fostered by Josie and Gary. Sarah would go on to work with [Amy Carlson](link_95) ("Josie" on AW) several more times: [Falcone (2000)](link_96), [Law & Order (1990)](link_97) and [Law & Order: Trial by Jury (2005)](link_98). Sarah was cast as one of the young "Audrey Hepburns" in [Jennifer Love Hewitt](link_99)'s [The Audrey Hepburn Story (2000)](link_100) the same year she was cast as "Molly" in ABC's [Annie (1999)](link_101) starring [Kathy Bates](link_102), [Audra McDonald](link_103), [Alan Cumming](link_104), [Victor Garber](link_105) and [Kristin Chenoweth](link_106), [Joe Gould's Secret (2000)](link_107) and [Falcone (2000)](link_96). Aside from all of her film and television work, Sarah studied voice, ballet, jazz, hip-hop, tap, Theatre Dance, and performed with her tap and Theatre dance class at "Reel to Real" at Lincoln Center as invited performers.  
  
A New York-born and raised girl, Sarah spent much of her time working in film, television, and voicing many radio ads, as well as traveling with her father, [Edward James Hyland](link_91), while he worked at many different theaters in the country. She was home schooled by her mother until 2nd grade and then attended Public School. In 6th Grade, she was accepted into PPAS (Professional Performing Arts School) where she stayed until she graduated in 2008. When Sarah turned 18, she moved to Los Angeles, CA and, within two weeks, had landed a pilot named "My American Family". Once picked up the name was changed to [Modern Family (2009)](link_108). To date, Sarah portrays "Haley Dunphy", the eldest Dunphy child. [Modern Family (2009)](link_108) has won multiple awards most notably the Emmy for Outstanding Comedy Series.  
  
Before moving to L.A., Sarah did a multitude of film and television and, at the age of 11 1/2, she made her stage debut at Papermill Playhouse in Millburn, NJ in the title role of "Annie". From there, Sarah added many more stage productions to her resume including "Bad Girls", "Dark Part of the Forest" and both productions on and off Broadway of "Grey Gardens" in the role of "Jackie Bouvier". "Grey Gardens" was nominated for Best Musical at the Tony Awards, and [Christine Ebersole](link_109) and [Mary Louise Wilson](link_110) won Best Actress and Best Supporting Actress Tony's for their work. [William Ivey Long](link_111) won for his costume design. Sarah also did many development workshops including: "A Little Princess", "Bye Bye Birdie', and "Shrek, the Musical", to name a few.  #### [1. Kay Panabaker](link_45) 

    *   Actress
    *   Additional Crew
    *   Soundtrack

[Fame (2009)](link_46)

Stephanie Kay Panabaker is an American actress, who was born on May 2, 1990 in Orange Grove, Texas, USA. She is the daughter of Donna (née Mayock) and Harold Panabaker. She has an older sister, [Danielle Panabaker](link_47), who is also an actress. She started acting at various community theaters in Chicago, Philadelphia and Atlanta. In Naperville, Illinois, Kay attended Crone Middle School for sixth grade, and moved to Los Angeles, California, at the start of seventh grade. In between projects, Kay focuses on her academics. She graduated from high school, as valedictorian, when she was thirteen-years-old and received her Associate's Degree at age fifteen. Kay received two academic scholarships from Glendale Community College, where she attended, studying acting, and where she was on the Dean's list, graduating with honors. She was accepted to the UCLA online program as a junior history major, when she was fifteen, and completed her online BA in History from UCLA, before she turned eighteen. Kay was inspired by an elementary school teacher, who made learning exciting, and she wants to do the same for others, hoping to teach 4th or 5th grade, once she finishes her teaching degree. Panabaker has guest-starred in several television dramas and soap operas. She portrayed "Alice Brand" in [7th Heaven (1996)](link_48); "Melissa Rue" in [ER (1994)](link_49); "Sara" in [Port Charles (1997)](link_50); "Carrie Bauer" in [The Brothers Garcia (2000)](link_51); "Elisha" in [Medium (2005)](link_52); "Lindsey Willows" in [CSI: Crime Scene Investigation (2000)](link_53); to name a few. In film, she appeared in [Dead Heat (2002)](link_54) as "Sam LaRoche"; and did some voice work in the Disney/Pixas film, [Monsters, Inc. (2001)](link_55). Panabaker's breakout role came when she starred in The WB's [Summerland (2004)](link_56) as "Nikki Westerly", in the 2004-2005 season. She also appeared as "Georgie" in [Nancy Drew (2007)](link_57), alongside [Emma Roberts](link_58) and [Amy Bruckner](link_59). She starred in the 2007 movie, [Moondance Alexander (2007)](link_60), along with actors, [Don Johnson](link_61), [Lori Loughlin](link_62), [James Best](link_63), [Sasha Cohen](link_64) and [Whitney Sloan](link_65). She co-starred on the ABC sci-fi series, [No Ordinary Family (2010)](link_66), along with actors [Michael Chiklis](link_67), [Julie Benz](link_68), [Jimmy Bennett](link_69), [Autumn Reeser](link_70), [Romany Malco](link_71) and [Stephen Collins](link_72).

 #### [2. Anna Maria Perez de Tagle](link_74) 

    *   Actress
    *   Soundtrack

[Fame (2009)](link_75)

Anna Maria Perez de Tagle was born on December 23, 1990 in San Francisco, California as Anna Maria Francesca Enriquez Perez de Tagle. She's 1 of today's hottest triple threats, w/ an extensive list of accomplishments like acting, singing & dancing. She has opened for the Jonas Brothers Asia tour in 2012 & starred in Godspell on Broadway. She has been featured on shows such as [Late Show with David Letterman (1993)](link_76), [The View (1997)](link_77)&[The Rosie Show (2011)](link_78). She was also featured in a sold-out concert that took place May 7, 2012 on board the Hornblower Hybrid in New York City, benefiting St. Jude Children's Research Hospital.  
  
She was voted Best Featured Female Artist in a Musical at the 2012 Broadway World Awards.  
  
She starred in [Camp Rock (2008)](link_79)&[Camp Rock 2: The Final Jam (2010)](link_80) as Ella, then guest starred in [Baby Daddy (2012)](link_81) as Jenna. She also had a recurring role in [Hannah Montana (2006)](link_82) as Ashley Dewitt.  
  
In 2009, she stole the screen in [Fame (2009)](link_83) as Joy. In 2010, she toured w/ [Demi Lovato](link_84)&[Jonas Brothers](link_85) in North as well as South America. She served as an opener & performer.  
  
At the Ronald Reagan Centennial Birthday Celebration, former 1st lady [Nancy Reagan](link_86) requested her to perform 2 of her favorite Broadway songs in front of hundreds of dignitaries at the Ronald Reagan Library: I Dreamed A Dream from Les Misérables & Someone Like You from Jekyll & Hyde.  
  
She enjoys working w/ the Children's Hospital of L.A., St. Jude's Research Hospital & the American Diabetes Association as well as singing, dancing, working out & reading.  
  
She resides in NYC & L.A.

Sarah Hyland was born in New York City to actors [Melissa D. Canaday](link_90) and [Edward James Hyland](link_91). She began in the business at the age of 4 with commercial work and voice overs. Her first film was [Private Parts (1997)](link_92). She then moved on to [The Object of My Affection (1998)](link_93) and then spent time on [Another World (1964)](link_94) as "Rain Wolfe", a child found in the park, and fostered by Josie and Gary. Sarah would go on to work with [Amy Carlson](link_95) ("Josie" on AW) several more times: [Falcone (2000)](link_96), [Law & Order (1990)](link_97) and [Law & Order: Trial by Jury (2005)](link_98). Sarah was cast as one of the young "Audrey Hepburns" in [Jennifer Love Hewitt](link_99)'s [The Audrey Hepburn Story (2000)](link_100) the same year she was cast as "Molly" in ABC's [Annie (1999)](link_101) starring [Kathy Bates](link_102), [Audra McDonald](link_103), [Alan Cumming](link_104), [Victor Garber](link_105) and [Kristin Chenoweth](link_106), [Joe Gould's Secret (2000)](link_107) and [Falcone (2000)](link_96). Aside from all of her film and television work, Sarah studied voice, ballet, jazz, hip-hop, tap, Theatre Dance, and performed with her tap and Theatre dance class at "Reel to Real" at Lincoln Center as invited performers.  
  
A New York-born and raised girl, Sarah spent much of her time working in film, television, and voicing many radio ads, as well as traveling with her father, [Edward James Hyland](link_91), while he worked at many different theaters in the country. She was home schooled by her mother until 2nd grade and then attended Public School. In 6th Grade, she was accepted into PPAS (Professional Performing Arts School) where she stayed until she graduated in 2008. When Sarah turned 18, she moved to Los Angeles, CA and, within two weeks, had landed a pilot named "My American Family". Once picked up the name was changed to [Modern Family (2009)](link_108). To date, Sarah portrays "Haley Dunphy", the eldest Dunphy child. [Modern Family (2009)](link_108) has won multiple awards most notably the Emmy for Outstanding Comedy Series.  
  
Before moving to L.A., Sarah did a multitude of film and television and, at the age of 11 1/2, she made her stage debut at Papermill Playhouse in Millburn, NJ in the title role of "Annie". From there, Sarah added many more stage productions to her resume including "Bad Girls", "Dark Part of the Forest" and both productions on and off Broadway of "Grey Gardens" in the role of "Jackie Bouvier". "Grey Gardens" was nominated for Best Musical at the Tony Awards, and [Christine Ebersole](link_109) and [Mary Louise Wilson](link_110) won Best Actress and Best Supporting Actress Tony's for their work. But while filming the show in 1996, her brother Rafael was murdered in a failed kidnapping attempt back in Colombia. That loss was what finally pushed her to move her entire family permanently to Miami. She went from a Univision travel show to the highest-paid actress on American television for seven consecutive years. Hosted by @hennasahota for History Photographed.

Stephanie Kay Panabaker is an American actress, who was born on May 2, 1990 in Orange Grove, Texas, USA. She is the daughter of Donna (née Mayock) and Harold Panabaker. She has an older sister, [Danielle Panabaker](link_52), who is also an actress. She started acting at various community theaters in Chicago, Philadelphia and Atlanta. In Naperville, Illinois, Kay attended Crone Middle School for sixth grade, and moved to Los Angeles, California, at the start of seventh grade. In between projects, Kay focuses on her academics. She graduated from high school, as valedictorian, when she was thirteen-years-old and received her Associate's Degree at age fifteen. Kay received two academic scholarships from Glendale Community College, where she attended, studying acting, and where she was on the Dean's list, graduating with honors. She was accepted to the UCLA online program as a junior history major, when she was fifteen, and completed her online BA in History from UCLA, before she turned eighteen. Kay was inspired by an elementary school teacher, who made learning exciting, and she wants to do the same for others, hoping to teach 4th or 5th grade, once she finishes her teaching degree. Panabaker has guest-starred in several television dramas and soap operas. She portrayed "Alice Brand" in [7th Heaven (1996)](link_53); "Melissa Rue" in [ER (1994)](link_54); "Sara" in [Port Charles (1997)](link_55); "Carrie Bauer" in [The Brothers Garcia (2000)](link_56); "Elisha" in [Medium (2005)](link_57); "Lindsey Willows" in [CSI: Crime Scene Investigation (2000)](link_58); to name a few. In film, she appeared in [Dead Heat (2002)](link_59) as "Sam LaRoche"; and did some voice work in the Disney/Pixas film, [Monsters, Inc. (2001)](link_60). Panabaker's breakout role came when she starred in The WB's [Summerland (2004)](link_61) as "Nikki Westerly", in the 2004-2005 season. She also appeared as "Georgie" in [Nancy Drew (2007)](link_62), alongside [Emma Roberts](link_63) and [Amy Bruckner](link_64). She starred in the 2007 movie, [Moondance Alexander (2007)](link_65), along with actors, [Don Johnson](link_66), [Lori Loughlin](link_67), [James Best](link_68), [Sasha Cohen](link_69) and [Whitney Sloan](link_70). She co-starred on the ABC sci-fi series, [No Ordinary Family (2010)](link_71), along with actors [Michael Chiklis](link_72), [Julie Benz](link_73), [Jimmy Bennett](link_74), [Autumn Reeser](link_75), [Romany Malco](link_76) and [Stephen Collins](link_77).

Anna Maria Perez de Tagle was born on December 23, 1990 in San Francisco, California as Anna Maria Francesca Enriquez Perez de Tagle. She's 1 of today's hottest triple threats, w/ an extensive list of accomplishments like acting, singing & dancing. She has opened for the Jonas Brothers Asia tour in 2012 & starred in Godspell on Broadway. She has been featured on shows such as [Late Show with David Letterman (1993)](link_51), [The View (1997)](link_52)&[The Rosie Show (2011)](link_53). She was also featured in a sold-out concert that took place May 7, 2012 on board the Hornblower Hybrid in New York City, benefiting St. Jude Children's Research Hospital.  
  
She was voted Best Featured Female Artist in a Musical at the 2012 Broadway World Awards.  
  
She starred in [Camp Rock (2008)](link_54)&[Camp Rock 2: The Final Jam (2010)](link_55) as Ella, then guest starred in [Baby Daddy (2012)](link_56) as Jenna. She also had a recurring role in [Hannah Montana (2006)](link_57) as Ashley Dewitt.  
  
In 2009, she stole the screen in [Fame (2009)](link_58) as Joy. In 2010, she toured w/ [Demi Lovato](link_59)&[Jonas Brothers](link_60) in North as well as South America. She served as an opener & performer.  
  
At the Ronald Reagan Centennial Birthday Celebration, former 1st lady [Nancy Reagan](link_61) requested her to perform 2 of her favorite Broadway songs in front of hundreds of dignitaries at the Ronald Reagan Library: I Dreamed A Dream from Les Misérables & Someone Like You from Jekyll & Hyde.  
  
She enjoys working w/ the Children's Hospital of L.A., St. Jude's Research Hospital & the American Diabetes Association as well as singing, dancing, working out & reading.  
  
She resides in NYC & L.A.
