Sarah Hyland was born in New York City to actors [Melissa D. Canaday](link_52) and [Edward James Hyland](link_53). She began in the business at the age of 4 with commercial work and voice overs. Her first film was [Private Parts (1997)](link_54). She then moved on to [The Object of My Affection (1998)](link_55) and then spent time on [Another World (1964)](link_56) as "Rain Wolfe", a child found in the park, and fostered by Josie and Gary. Sarah would go on to work with [Amy Carlson](link_57) ("Josie" on AW) several more times: [Falcone (2000)](link_58), [Law & Order (1990)](link_59) and [Law & Order: Trial by Jury (2005)](link_60). Sarah was cast as one of the young "Audrey Hepburns" in [Jennifer Love Hewitt](link_61)'s [The Audrey Hepburn Story (2000)](link_62) the same year she was cast as "Molly" in ABC's [Annie (1999)](link_63) starring [Kathy Bates](link_64), [Audra McDonald](link_65), [Alan Cumming](link_66), [Victor Garber](link_67) and [Kristin Chenoweth](link_68), [Joe Gould's Secret (2000)](link_69) and [Falcone (2000)](link_58). Aside from all of her film and television work, Sarah studied voice, ballet, jazz, hip-hop, tap, Theatre Dance, and performed with her tap and Theatre dance class at "Reel to Real" at Lincoln Center as invited performers.  
  
A New York-born and raised girl, Sarah spent much of her time working in film, television, and voicing many radio ads, as well as traveling with her father, [Edward James Hyland](link_53), while he worked at many different theaters in the country. She was home schooled by her mother until 2nd grade and then attended Public School. In 6th Grade, she was accepted into PPAS (Professional Performing Arts School) where she stayed until she graduated in 2008. When Sarah turned 18, she moved to Los Angeles, CA and, within two weeks, had landed a pilot named "My American Family". Once picked up the name was changed to [Modern Family (2009)](link_70). To date, Sarah portrays "Haley Dunphy", the eldest Dunphy child. [Modern Family (2009)](link_70) has won multiple awards most notably the Emmy for Outstanding Comedy Series.  
  
Before moving to L.A., Sarah did a multitude of film and television and, at the age of 11 1/2, she made her stage debut at Papermill Playhouse in Millburn, NJ in the title role of "Annie". From there, Sarah added many more stage productions to her resume including "Bad Girls", "Dark Part of the Forest" and both productions on and off Broadway of "Grey Gardens" in the role of "Jackie Bouvier". "Grey Gardens" was nominated for Best Musical at the Tony Awards, and [Christine Ebersole](link_71) and [Mary Louise Wilson](link_72) won Best Actress and Best Supporting Actress Tony's for their work. [William Ivey Long](link_73) won for his costume design. Sarah also did many development workshops including: "A Little Princess", "Bye Bye Birdie', and "Shrek, the Musical", to name a few. Sarah has worked with some of the top talent in the Industry: [Tim Robbins](link_74), [Stanley Tucci](link_75), [Ian Holmes](link_76), [Steve Martin](link_77), [John Turturro](link_78), [Hope Davis](link_79), [Keir Dullea](link_80), [Frances Fisher](link_81), [Brooke Shields](link_82), [Kim Raver](link_83), [Lindsay Price](link_84), [Timothy Busfield](link_85), among so many other incredible talents. She has guest starred on [Touched by an Angel (1994)](link_86), [Law & Order: Trial by Jury (2005)](link_60) and twice on [Law & Order: Special Victims Unit (1999)](link_87). Her second turn on [Hothouse (2009)](link_88) gave her a breakthrough role where she portrayed "Jennifer Banks", a student at a school for the gifted who kills her roommate in a drug fueled rage.  
  
Her work on [Lipstick Jungle (2008)](link_89) as [Brooke Shields](link_82)'s daughter further showcased her talent and, because of LJ's cancellation, drew her to Los Angeles and the role of "Haley Dunphy" on [Modern Family (2009)](link_70).  
  
Sarah has a maltipoo named Barkley, and is happily living in the Los Angeles Area. She is the Face of "Wallflower Jeans". Sarah's brother, [Ian Donovan Hyland](link_90), is also an actor and, even though most think Ian is her older brother, he is really 4 years her junior. Her father is a stage and film actor based in New York, and her mother is an acting coach to young actors.

## [ROCK DUO AIR SUPPLY WILL BE HONORED BY THE HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE WITH STAR ON THE HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME](link_12)

Air Supply will be honored with the 2,859th star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame on October 8th at 11:30 am PT at 6126 Hollywood Boulevard. Air Supply will receive their star in the category of Recording.

[Continue reading](link_12)

![Image 3: HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE TO HONOR ACTOR BRADLEY WHITFORD WITH STAR ON THE HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME](https://walkoffame.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/IMG_6297.jpg)

## [HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE TO HONOR ACTOR BRADLEY WHITFORD WITH STAR ON THE HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME](link_13)

Bradley Whitford will be honored with the 2,858th star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame on September 30th at 11:30 am PT at 6104 Hollywood Boulevard. Whitford will receive his star in the category of Television.

[Continue reading](link_13)

![Image 4: HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE TO HONOR ACTRESS NIA LONG WITH STAR ON THE HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME](https://walkoffame.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Nia-Long-Headshot-scaled.jpg)

## [HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE TO HONOR ACTRESS NIA LONG WITH STAR ON THE HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME](link_14)

Nia Long will be honored with the 2,857th star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame on September 16th at 11:30 am PT. Long will receive her star in the category of Motion Pictures.

[Continue reading](link_14)

![Image 5: HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE TO HONOR TELEVISION CREATIVE GREG DANIELS WITH STAR ON THE HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME](https://walkoffame.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Screenshot-2026-07-17-at-11.59.44-AM.png)

## [HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE TO HONOR TELEVISION CREATIVE GREG DANIELS WITH STAR ON THE HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME](link_15)

Greg Daniels will be honored with the 2,856th star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame on September 10th at 11:30 am PT at 6357 Hollywood Boulevard. Daniels will receive his star in the category of Television.

[Continue reading](link_15)

![Image 6: HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE TO HONOR BROADWAY STAR LEA SALONGA WITH A HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME STAR – MAKING HER THE FIRST FILIPINA TO BE HONORED WITH THE COVETED HOLLYWOOD STAR](https://walkoffame.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/E5400259-E3DF-41D2-BA9C-CF83731DFED9.jpeg)

## [HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE TO HONOR BROADWAY STAR LEA SALONGA WITH A HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME STAR – MAKING HER THE FIRST FILIPINA TO BE HONORED WITH THE COVETED HOLLYWOOD STAR](link_16)

Lea Salonga will be honored with the 2,855th star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame on September 4th at 11:30 am PT at 6255 Hollywood Boulevard. Salonga, will receive her star in the category of Live Performance.

[Continue reading](link_16)

![Image 7: HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE TO HONOR MUSICIAN ANGÉLIQUE KIDJO WITH STAR ON THE WALK OF FAME – MAKING HER THE FIRST AFRICAN MUSICIAN AND FIRST BLACK AFRICAN TO RECEIVE A COVETED STAR](https://walkoffame.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/MM0553_AK_PORTRAITS_241108AK-0219_editfinal_V1D_CREDIT_BRANTLEYGUTIERREZ-scaled.jpg)

## [HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE TO HONOR MUSICIAN ANGÉLIQUE KIDJO WITH STAR ON THE WALK OF FAME – MAKING HER THE FIRST AFRICAN MUSICIAN AND FIRST BLACK AFRICAN TO RECEIVE A COVETED STAR](link_17)

Five-time GRAMMY-winning musician Angélique Kidjo will be honored with the 2,854th star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame on August 18 at 11:30 am PT at 7011 Hollywood Boulevard, across the street from the historic Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel. Kidjo will receive her star in the category of Recording.

[Continue reading](link_17)

![Image 8: BATTER UP! HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE TO HONOR DODGER GREAT OREL HERSHISER WITH STAR ON THE HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME](https://walkoffame.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/DSC07870_2-scaled.jpg)

## [BATTER UP! HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE TO HONOR DODGER GREAT OREL HERSHISER WITH STAR ON THE HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME](link_18)

Orel Hershiser will be honored with the 2,853rd star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame on August 13th at 11:30 am PT at 6755 Hollywood Boulevard. Hershiser will receive his star in the category of Sports Entertainment.

[Continue reading](link_18)

AND HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE PRESIDENT & CEO RON FRIERSON DURING LIVE PRESS CONFERENCE AT FUNKO HOLLYWOOD](https://walkoffame.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Class-of-2027-Placeholder-02.png)

## [HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME CLASS OF 2027 ANNOUNCED BY WALK OF FAMERS MING-NA WEN AND SHEILA E.](link_19)

A new group of entertainment professionals in the categories of Motion Pictures, Television, Live Theatre/Live Performance, Radio, Recording and Sports Entertainment have been selected to receive stars on the Hollywood Walk of Fame by the Walk of Fame Selection Committee of the Hollywood Chamber of Commerce.

[Continue reading](link_19)

![Image 10: HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME CLASS OF 2027 TO BE ANNOUNCED BY WALK OF FAMERS MING-NA WEN AND SHEILA E. AND HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE PRESIDENT & CEO RON FRIERSON DURING LIVE PRESS CONFERENCE AT FUNKO HOLLYWOOD](https://walkoffame.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Class-of-2027-Placeholder-02.png)

## [HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME CLASS OF 2027 TO BE ANNOUNCED BY WALK OF FAMERS MING-NA WEN AND SHEILA E. AND HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE PRESIDENT & CEO RON FRIERSON DURING LIVE PRESS CONFERENCE AT FUNKO HOLLYWOOD](link_20)

A new group of 32 entertainment professionals in the categories of Motion Pictures, Television, Live Theatre/Live Performance, Radio, Recording, and Sports Entertainment have been selected to receive stars on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

[Continue reading](link_20)

![Image 11: HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE TO HONOR REGIONAL MEXICAN ACT INTOCABLE WITH STAR ON THE HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME     LA CAMARA DE COMERCIO DE HOLLYWOOD HOMENAJEARA A INTOCABLE CON UNA ESTRELLA EN EL PASEO DE LA FAMA DE HOLLYWOOD](https://walkoffame.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Nikon-1241-scaled.png)

## [HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE TO HONOR REGIONAL MEXICAN ACT INTOCABLE WITH STAR ON THE HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME LA CAMARA DE COMERCIO DE HOLLYWOOD HOMENAJEARA A INTOCABLE CON UNA ESTRELLA EN EL PASEO DE LA FAMA DE HOLLYWOOD](link_21)

Intocable will be honored with the 2,852nd star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame on Thursday, July 16, at 11:30 am PT. The star will be dedicated at 7083 Hollywood Boulevard. Intocable will receive their star in the category of Recording.

[Continue reading](link_21)

URL Source: https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://muse.ai/&h=AUCnjz3by_N9PgCIcxEF7y-Yg509IB1BPvhKa8CbgEYAI4HXQ0ndfHxjyqTzYkxMHuKuqhljeyoV34iRC1YIadcYg-Ej1BOC-mdzTxOZVM02EzZLB75spVzIGc6sCMNA4a9o8BV_Oy8Jng

Log in

![Image 1: Muse](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/brand/muse-logo.svg)
# Muse, AI that gets it done for you Muse[Video 1](https://l.facebook.com/videos/avatars/hatch_connecting.mp4)[Video 2](https://l.facebook.com/videos/avatars/hatch_working.mp4), AI that gets it done for you sorts your email books reservations shops for you saves you money manages calendars builds fitness plans gets it done for you sorts your email![Image 2](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-envelope.webp)books reservations![Image 3](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-airplane.webp)shops for you![Image 4](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-cart.webp)saves you money![Image 5](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-piggybank.webp)manages calendars![Image 6](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-calendar.webp)builds fitness plans![Image 7](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/b-01.webp)gets it done for you

# Log in or create an account

Mobile number or email(required) 

You may receive SMS notifications from us by using your mobile number. [Learn more](https://www.meta.com/help/artificial-intelligence/31983416211257755/)

Continue

[Learn more](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://muse.ai/&h=AUCnjz3by_N9PgCIcxEF7y-Yg509IB1BPvhKa8CbgEYAI4HXQ0ndfHxjyqTzYkxMHuKuqhljeyoV34iRC1YIadcYg-Ej1BOC-mdzTxOZVM02EzZLB75spVzIGc6sCMNA4a9o8BV_Oy8Jng#landing-introduction-video-title)

## Built around your whole life

Give Muse a goal or task and it handles the rest, from saving money and improving your health to smart shopping and helping you strengthen your relationships.

[Video 3](https://scontent.xx.fbcdn.net/o1/v/t6/f2/m421/AQPvdntV2G814fVexG62mHy9MLAFz-IUx2_276pwlTOScjlG7403bT1NxrxgW2yToPZR5BOsHoRWgC3EQGGX.mp4?_nc_sid=9c7e41&_nc_ht=scontent.xx.fbcdn.net&ccb=17-1&_nc_gid=MCMYUU3rNxCn_cGtNNANzw&edm=AIlawRcEAAAA&_nc_zt=28&oh=00_AQPEEnqjh0vAi86k65me-OOmlmDLs7EjSr9vFEQVCqefOw&oe=6AEA57AE#t=1)

### Every Muse user shares their own computer in the cloud with their Muse.

Muse Secure VM is a persistent, isolated Linux computer with a full browser that you and your agent can use to complete tasks, allowing you to intervene at any point. It's your computer and your browser, with the storage, CPU, and memory to handle real work.

![Image 8: Floating browser, search, map, calendar, and confirmation panels](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/browser.webp)![Image 9: Floating browser, search, map, calendar, and confirmation panels](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/browser-dark.webp)

### Designed around the way you already communicate

Chat with your agent in the same way you message with other people, using the Muse app on mobile, Mac, or directly in WhatsApp. There's no learning curve, just tell Muse what you want to get done.

![Image 10: A chat on a phone where the agent has filled out a school form, shown beside a laptop](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/messaging.webp)![Image 11: A chat on a phone where the agent has filled out a school form, shown beside a laptop](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/messaging-dark.webp)

### Stay in control of what your agent does

Approve actions your agent takes on your behalf before they happen, like sending emails and making purchases. See a complete audit trail of everything your agent has done (and what it's planning to do).

![Image 12: Floating purchase, message, activity, permission, and decision controls](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/approvals.webp)![Image 13: Floating purchase, message, activity, permission, and decision controls](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/approvals-dark.webp)

### Your data is kept secure and private

Save your logins to a secure credential store Muse can't see, with 1Password integration coming soon. When shopping, a one-time card number is generated at checkout so your real card stays hidden from the merchant and your agent. Eligible purchases are covered by [Link's purchase protections](https://link.com/protections), a first for AI agents, and your conversations are not shared with Meta's ad systems.

![Image 14: A vault, privacy shield, masked credential, security control, and virtual card](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/secure-storage.webp)![Image 15: A vault, privacy shield, masked credential, security control, and virtual card](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/secure-storage-dark.webp)

### Proactively helps with your goals and suggests ideas

Muse helps you stay on top of things, takes tasks and projects off your plate, and turns long-term goals into real progress. It learns from conversations, reflects on what matters and gets sharper, coming back with ideas built around what you actually need, ready to act on them under your direction.

![Image 16: Floating checklist, calendar, route, progress, and idea panels](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/goals.webp)![Image 17: Floating checklist, calendar, route, progress, and idea panels](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/goals-dark.webp)

### Connects to your apps and builds its own tools

Connect the apps you use daily, like email, calendar, and Instagram. You decide what your agent can see and what it can do. If a task needs a tool that doesn't exist, your agent builds it for you.

![Image 18: Connected app, messaging, media, cloud, calendar, and automation tiles](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/connectors.webp)

## Get the most out of your Muse

A guided tour of Muse, from setting a first goal to seeing it through.

![Image 19: Product designer presenting a guided tour of Muse](https://l.facebook.com/images/hatch/landing/product-walkthrough-cover.png)

## Learn more about Muse

Explore the choices behind Muse and how it is built to deserve your trust.

### [How We Designed Muse When Muse works, it feels like magic. These are the product choices that make the experience possible.](https://introducing.muse.ai/)### [How We Built Safety Into Muse Muse is built for privacy, safety, and security. Learn how these principles shape every part of the product.](https://security.muse.ai/)### [Muse for Business Meet the AI agent that works for your small business and keeps jobs moving between your decisions.](https://l.facebook.com/business)

## Ready to try Muse?

Log in

[](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000906/bio/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_sm)

Annette Bening was born on May 29, 1958 in Topeka, Kansas, the youngest of four children. Her family moved to California when she was young, and she grew up there. She graduated from San Francisco State University and began her acting career with the American Conservatory Theatre in San Francisco, eventually moving to New York where she acted on the stage (including a Tony-award nomination in 1987 for her work in the Broadway play "Coastal Disturbances") and got her first film roles, in a few TV movies.  
  
As is so often the case, her first big-screen role was in a forgettable movie, this one [The Great Outdoors (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0095253/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), in which she had little screen time. However, her next work onscreen was in [Miloš Forman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001232/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s [Valmont (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0098575/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), a film adaptation of [Choderlos de Laclos](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0480166/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)' "Les Liaisons Dangereuses". Unfortunately, de Laclos' story had also just served as the source of a more Hollywoodized and successful movie version, [Dangerous Liaisons (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094947/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), which had been released the previous year, and Foreman's treatment went little noticed. Bening's career turned an important corner the following year when she co-starred with [Anjelica Huston](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001378/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [John Cusack](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000131/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) in [Stephen Frears](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001241/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s powerful, entertaining screen adaptation of [Jim Thompson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0860292/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s novel [The Grifters (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0099703/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and her artful turn as a con artist gained her the first of several Academy award nominations. On the strength of this performance [Warren Beatty](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000886/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) cast Bening as [Virginia Hill](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1389800/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Bugsy Siegel](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1179222/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s fiery actress moll, in his [Bugsy (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0101516/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), the story of Siegel's founding of Las Vegas. Although the movie itself did not fare well, it resulted in a relationship with Beatty which led to Bening's pregnancy and then her marriage to Beatty in 1992 - it was the second marriage for Bening, who had been separated from her first husband since 1986 but did not finalize her divorce until 1991. The couple then collaborated on the extravagant flop [Love Affair (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0110391/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), though the next year her career rebounded with her turn as Queen Elizabeth in the highly-regarded 1995 production of [Richard III (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0114279/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Notable performances have since included an obsessive, pushy real estate agent in [American Beauty (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0169547/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and as the eponymous character in [István Szabó](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0843640/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s screen adaptation of the [W. Somerset Maugham](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0560857/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) novel [Being Julia (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0340012/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) - both were duly noted by the Academy, with Oscar nominations.  
  
Bening has great poise and screen presence and, at her best, can turn in a very strong performance. Although her resume often features long stretches of mediocre productions before the next good part turns up, when it does, it proves worth the wait. Bening has four children with Beatty.

**[Annette Carol Bening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette%20Bening "w:Annette Bening")** (born [29 May](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/29_May "29 May")[1958](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/1958 "1958")) is an American actress. In a career spanning over four decades, she has received [various accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20awards%20and%20nominations%20received%20by%20Annette%20Bening "w:List of awards and nominations received by Annette Bening"), including a [BAFTA Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British%20Academy%20Film%20Award "w:British Academy Film Award") and two [Golden Globes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden%20Globes "w:Golden Globes") as well as nominations for a [Primetime Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime%20Emmy%20Award "w:Primetime Emmy Award"), two [Tony Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony%20Awards "w:Tony Awards"), and four [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy%20Awards "w:Academy Awards").

 #### [1. Annette Bening](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000906/?ref_=sr_t_1) 

    *   Actress
    *   Producer
    *   Soundtrack

[American Beauty (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0169547/?ref_=sr_knf_1)

Annette Bening was born on May 29, 1958 in Topeka, Kansas, the youngest of four children. Her family moved to California when she was young, and she grew up there. She graduated from San Francisco State University and began her acting career with the American Conservatory Theatre in San Francisco, eventually moving to New York where she acted on the stage (including a Tony-award nomination in 1987 for her work in the Broadway play "Coastal Disturbances") and got her first film roles, in a few TV movies.  
  
As is so often the case, her first big-screen role was in a forgettable movie, this one [The Great Outdoors (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0095253/?ref_=sr), in which she had little screen time. However, her next work onscreen was in [Miloš Forman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001232/?ref_=sr)'s [Valmont (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0098575/?ref_=sr), a film adaptation of [Choderlos de Laclos](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0480166/?ref_=sr)' "Les Liaisons Dangereuses". Unfortunately, de Laclos' story had also just served as the source of a more Hollywoodized and successful movie version, [Dangerous Liaisons (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094947/?ref_=sr), which had been released the previous year, and Foreman's treatment went little noticed. Bening's career turned an important corner the following year when she co-starred with [Anjelica Huston](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001378/?ref_=sr) and [John Cusack](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000131/?ref_=sr) in [Stephen Frears](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001241/?ref_=sr)'s powerful, entertaining screen adaptation of [Jim Thompson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0860292/?ref_=sr)'s novel [The Grifters (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0099703/?ref_=sr), and her artful turn as a con artist gained her the first of several Academy award nominations. On the strength of this performance [Warren Beatty](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000886/?ref_=sr) cast Bening as [Virginia Hill](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1389800/?ref_=sr), [Bugsy Siegel](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1179222/?ref_=sr)'s fiery actress moll, in his [Bugsy (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0101516/?ref_=sr), the story of Siegel's founding of Las Vegas. Although the movie itself did not fare well, it resulted in a relationship with Beatty which led to Bening's pregnancy and then her marriage to Beatty in 1992 - it was the second marriage for Bening, who had been separated from her first husband since 1986 but did not finalize her divorce until 1991. The couple then collaborated on the extravagant flop [Love Affair (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0110391/?ref_=sr), though the next year her career rebounded with her turn as Queen Elizabeth in the highly-regarded 1995 production of [Richard III (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0114279/?ref_=sr). Notable performances have since included an obsessive, pushy real estate agent in [American Beauty (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0169547/?ref_=sr), and as the eponymous character in [István Szabó](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0843640/?ref_=sr)'s screen adaptation of the [W. Somerset Maugham](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0560857/?ref_=sr) novel [Being Julia (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0340012/?ref_=sr) - both were duly noted by the Academy, with Oscar nominations.  
  
Bening has great poise and screen presence and, at her best, can turn in a very strong performance. Although her resume often features long stretches of mediocre productions before the next good part turns up, when it does, it proves worth the wait. Bening has four children with Beatty.

 #### [2. Michael Douglas](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000140/?ref_=sr_t_2) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Director

[Wall Street (1987)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094291/?ref_=sr_knf_2)

A legendary actor with 50 celebrated years of film, television and producing experience, Michael Douglas is known for his era-defining roles and enduring cultural impact.  
  
In addition to his career accomplishments, Douglas has remained a steadfast public servant, activist and philanthropist dedicated to peace and human welfare, democracy, gun control advocacy, support of the arts and support of nuclear disarmament. In 1998, former United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan appointed Douglas as a Messenger of Peace for his commitment on disarmament issues, including nuclear non-proliferation and halting the illicit trade in small arms and light weapons.  
  
Since his earliest acting work on [Hail, Hero! (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064399/?ref_=sr) and [The Streets of San Francisco (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068135/?ref_=sr) Douglas has played some of the most memorable and enigmatic American anti-heroes of the last half century. He is most known for his iconic screen roles, like his Academy Award-winning turn as Gordon Gekko [Wall Street (1987)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094291/?ref_=sr) as well as the critically and commercially acclaimed films [Fatal Attraction (1987)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0093010/?ref_=sr), [The American President (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0112346/?ref_=sr), [Basic Instinct (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0103772/?ref_=sr), [Traffic (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0181865/?ref_=sr) and [Romancing the Stone (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0088011/?ref_=sr). He is also a prolific producer with credits on politically relevant and socially influential motion pictures like [One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0073486/?ref_=sr), [The China Syndrome (1979)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0078966/?ref_=sr), [Traffic (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0181865/?ref_=sr) the television series: [The Kominsky Method (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt7255502/?ref_=sr) and an upcoming limited series where Douglas portrays Benjamin [Franklin (2024)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt18351584/?ref_=sr) during his nine years in France lobbying for French aid for the American Revolution.  
  
With a passion for complex protagonists and darkly humorous undercurrents, Douglas has received numerous accolades for his work, including two Academy Awards, five Golden Globe Awards, a Primetime Emmy Award, AFI Life Achievement Award, two French César Awards for Career Achievement and, most recently, the Palme d'or d'honneur for lifetime achievement at the 76th Annual Festival de Cannes as well as the Satyajit Ray Lifetime Achievement Award for Excellence in Cinema at the Goa Film Festival in India.  
  
Michael Douglas was born in New Brunswick, New Jersey, to actors [Diana Douglas](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0235022/?ref_=sr) (Diana Love Dill) and [Kirk Douglas](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000018/?ref_=sr) (born Issur Danielovitch). His paternal grandparents were Belarusian Jewish immigrants, while his mother was born in Bermuda, the daughter of a local Attorney General, Lieutenant Colonel Thomas Melville Dill; Diana's family had long been established in both Bermuda and the United States. Douglas's parents divorced when he was six, and he went to live with his mother and her new husband. Only seeing Kirk on holidays, Michael attended Eaglebrook School in Deerfield, Massachusetts, where he was about a year younger than all of his classmates.  
  
Douglas attended the elite preparatory Choate School and spent his summers with his father on movie sets. Although accepted at Yale, Douglas attended the University of California, Santa Barbara. Deciding he wanted to be an actor in his teenage years, Michael often asked his father about getting a "foot in the door" Kirk was strongly opposed to Michael pursuing an acting career, saying that it was an industry with many downs and few ups, and that he wanted all four of his sons to stay out of it. Michael, however, was persistent, and made his film debut in his father's film [Cast a Giant Shadow (1966)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0060218/?ref_=sr).  
  
After receiving his B.A. degree in 1968, Douglas moved to New York City to continue his dramatic training, studying at the American Place Theatre with [Wynn Handman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0359640/?ref_=sr), and at the Neighborhood Playhouse, where he appeared in workshop productions of Pirandello's Six Characters in Search of an Author (1976) and [Thornton Wilder](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0928642/?ref_=sr)'s Happy Journey (1963). A few months after he arrived in New York, Douglas got his first big break, when he was cast in the pivotal role of the free-spirited scientist who compromises his liberal views to accept a lucrative job with a high-tech chemical corporation in the CBS Playhouse production of [Ellen M. Violett](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0899225/?ref_=sr)'s drama, The Experiment, which was televised nationwide on February 25, 1969.  
  
Douglas' convincing portrayal won him the leading role in the adaptation of John Weston's controversial novel, [Hail, Hero! (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064399/?ref_=sr), which was the initial project of CBS's newly organized theatrical film production company, Cinema Center Films. Douglas starred as a well-meaning, almost saintly young pacifist determined not only to justify his beliefs to his conservative parents but also to test them under fire in the jungles of Indochina. His second feature, [Adam at Six A.M. (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065371/?ref_=sr) concerned a young man's search for his roots. Douglas next appeared in the film version of [Ron Cowen](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0184734/?ref_=sr)'s play [Summertree (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0067804/?ref_=sr), produced by 'Kirk Douglas'' Bryna Company, and then [Napoleon and Samantha (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068990/?ref_=sr), a sentimental children's melodrama from the Walt Disney studio.  
  
In between film assignments, he worked in summer stock and off-Broadway productions, among them "City Scenes," [Frank Gagliano](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3422900/?ref_=sr)'s surrealistic vignettes of contemporary life in New York, [John Patrick Shanley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0788234/?ref_=sr)'s short-lived romance "Love is a Time of Day" and [George Tabori](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0846068/?ref_=sr)'s "Pinkville," in which he played a young innocent brutalized by his military training. He also appeared in the made-for-television thriller, "When Michael Calls," broadcast by ABC-TV on February 5, 1972 and in episodes of the popular series "Medical Center" and "The F.B.I."  
  
Impressed by Douglas' performance in a segment of The F.B.I. (1965), producer 'Quinn Martin' signed the actor for the part of [Karl Malden](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001500/?ref_=sr)'s sidekick in the police series "The Streets of San Francisco", which premiered in September 1972 and became one of ABC's highest-rated prime-time programs in the mid-1970s. Douglas earned three successive Emmy Award nominations for his performance and he directed two episodes of the series.  
  
During the annual breaks in the shooting schedule for The Streets of San Francisco (1972), Douglas devoted most of his time to his film production company, Big Stick Productions, Ltd., which produced several short subjects in the early 1970s. Long interested in producing a film version of [Ken Kesey](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0450181/?ref_=sr)'s grimly humorous novel [One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0073486/?ref_=sr), Douglas purchased the movie rights from his father and began looking for financial backing. After a number of major motion picture studios turned him down, Douglas formed a partnership with [Saul Zaentz](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0951763/?ref_=sr), a record industry executive, and the two set about recruiting the cast and crew. Douglas still had a year to go on his contract for "The Streets of San Francisco," but the producers agreed to write his character out of the story so that he could concentrate on filming "Cuckoo's Nest."  
  
A critical and commercial success, [One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0073486/?ref_=sr) won five Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Best Director, Best Screenplay, Best Actor and Best Actress, and went on to gross more than $180 million at the box office. Douglas suddenly found himself in demand as an independent producer. One of the many scripts submitted to him for consideration was Mike Gray's chilling account of the attempted cover-up of an accident at a nuclear power plant. Attracted by the combination of social relevance and suspense, Douglas immediately bought the property. Deemed not commercial by most investors, Douglas teamed up with Jane Fonda and her own motion picture production company, IPC Films.  
  
A Michael Douglas-IPC Films co-production, [The China Syndrome (1979)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0078966/?ref_=sr) starred [Jack Lemmon](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000493/?ref_=sr),

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

## From today's featured article

[![Image 4: Pennsylvania State Capitol](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Flying_the_Pride_Flag_over_the_Capitol_%2850035197647%29.jpg/250px-Flying_the_Pride_Flag_over_the_Capitol_%2850035197647%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flying_the_Pride_Flag_over_the_Capitol_(50035197647).jpg "Pennsylvania State Capitol")

The **[Pennsylvania State Capitol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania_State_Capitol "Pennsylvania State Capitol")** is located in [Harrisburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrisburg,_Pennsylvania "Harrisburg, Pennsylvania"). The building was designed by [Joseph Miller Huston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Miller_Huston "Joseph Miller Huston") and completed in 1906 in a [Beaux-Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beaux-Arts_architecture "Beaux-Arts architecture") style with decorative [Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance_Revival_architecture "Renaissance Revival architecture") themes. It houses the legislative chambers for the [Pennsylvania General Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania_General_Assembly "Pennsylvania General Assembly"), the Harrisburg chambers for the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Pennsylvania "Supreme Court of Pennsylvania") and [Superior Court of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superior_Court_of_Pennsylvania "Superior Court of Pennsylvania"), and the offices of [the state's governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_Pennsylvania "List of governors of Pennsylvania") and [lieutenant governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_Governor_of_Pennsylvania "Lieutenant Governor of Pennsylvania"). The capitol project was the subject of a [graft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graft_(politics) "Graft (politics)") scandal, as the construction and furnishing cost three times more than the General Assembly had appropriated for the project. The Pennsylvania State Capitol is often referred to as a "palace of art" because of its many sculptures, murals, and stained-glass windows, most of which are Pennsylvania-themed or were made in Pennsylvania. The building was listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places "National Register of Historic Places") in 1977 and designated a [National Historic Landmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Historic_Landmark "National Historic Landmark") in 2006. _(**[Full article...](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania\_State\_Capitol "Pennsylvania State Capitol")**)_

## HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE TO HONOR ACTRESS NIA LONG WITH STAR ON THE HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME

![Image 2](https://walkoffame.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Nia-Long-Headshot-scaled.jpg)
WHO | HONOREE Nia Long

EMCEE Variety correspondent Angelique Jackson

GUEST SPEAKERS Graham King, Snoop Dogg

WHAT Dedication of the 2,857th star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame

WHEN: Wednesday, September 16th, 2026 at 11:30 AM PT

WHERE:6150 Hollywood Boulevard

WATCH LIVE: The event will be streamed live exclusively at www.walkoffame.com

Nia Long will be honored with the 2,857th star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame on September 16th at 11:30 am PT. Long will receive her star in the category of Motion Pictures. Joining emcee Angelique Jackson will be _Michael_ producer Graham King, and Snoop Dogg.

The Hollywood Chamber of Commerce administers the legendary Walk of Fame for the City of Los Angeles and has proudly hosted the globally iconic star ceremonies for decades. Millions of people from here and around the world have visited this cultural landmark since 1960.

**ABOUT OUR HONOREE**

“The Hollywood Chamber of Commerce is proud to welcome Nia Long to the Hollywood Walk of Fame," stated Ana Martinez, Walk of Fame producer. “Nia is such a beloved and talented actress, and we’re so excited to celebrate her incredible career with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. She has brought so many unforgettable characters to life and has connected with audiences for decades. It’s wonderful to see her receive this well-deserved honor,” added Martinez.

Nia Long is an award-winning actor known for her iconic work and legendary roles across both film and television.

Long’s most recent film sees her starring in _Michael_, the blockbuster biopic of cultural icon Michael Jackson, which was released by Lionsgate on April 24, 2026 to massive global box office success. The film scored the top launch ever for a music biopic domestically, and recently dethroned _Oppenheimer_ as the highest-grossing biopic of all time globally as it joined the billion-dollar club and became the top-grossing film worldwide in the history of Lionsgate._Michael_ was directed by Antoine Fuqua, and produced by Academy Award-winning _Bohemian Rhapsody_ producer Graham King. The film starred Long as Katherine Jackson, matriarch of the Jackson family, alongside Colman Domingo as Joe Jackson, and Jaafar Jackson, Michael Jackson’s nephew, as the music icon.

A four-time NAACP Award winner, her role in _Boyz n the Hood_ in the 90’s put her on the map, followed by iconic parts in _Friday_,_The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air_,_Third Watch_, Tyler Perry’s _The Single Moms Club_,_Made in America_,_NCIS: Los Angeles_,_Empire_,_#blackAF_, and _Dear White People_, among others.

Up next, Long recently wrapped production for Netflix’s upcoming romantic drama _Don’t Ever Wonder_. Reuniting with her beloved _Love Jones_ co-star Larenz Tate, the film is inspired by Maxwell’s _Urban Hang Suite_ album, and Long also serves as Executive Producer. It was just announced that Long and Ice Cube are reuniting after 20 years for _Are They Gone Yet?_, which is currently in early development after being acquired by Skydance Sports, two decades after the pair starred alongside each other in the hit films _Are We There Yet?_ and _Are We Done Yet?_

Long’s other films include:_You People,_ _Missing_,_Searching,_ _Fatal Affair_, and _The Banker_, along with _The Best Man: The Final Chapters_, which premiered to record ratings, reuniting the original cast once again to send this decades-long franchise off in style and earning her a 2023 NAACP Award.

Long’s upcoming memoir will be published by Gallery Books, and in 2024 she was a Grammy nominee, appearing on Janelle Monáe’s _The Age of Pleasure_, which was nominated for Album of The Year.

She is a longtime supporter of the United Nations Foundation and in 2023 was honored by Reel Works with the ChangeMaker Award.

**THE HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE’S WALK OF FAME**

The Hollywood Walk of Fame is a celebration of art, entertainment, and all things Hollywood. Star ceremonies are broadcast worldwide, connecting fans with their favorite artists. The Hollywood Chamber of Commerce administers the Walk of Fame on behalf of the City of Los Angeles. Honorees are selected by a committee of their peers. Sponsors fund the star, the ceremony, and the maintenance of the legendary attraction. The Walk of Fame is free to all. To learn more and find your favorite stars, visit www.walkoffame.com.

**Hollywood Walk of Fame contact: Ana Martinez, Ana@hollywoodchamber.net**

**ABOUT THE HOLLYWOOD CHAMBER OF COMMERCE (HCC)**

Founded in 1921, the Hollywood Chamber of Commerce is dedicated to advancing the economic vitality, cultural richness, and civic well-being of Hollywood. Representing nearly 700 member organizations that collectively employ more than 148,000 people, the Chamber is Hollywood's largest and most influential business organization.

As the leading advocate for Hollywood's business community, the Chamber convenes leaders across industries to champion initiatives that strengthen the local economy, enhance quality of life, and elevate Hollywood's position as the world's premier destination for entertainment, tourism, investment, and innovation.

The Chamber is also the proud steward of two of the world's most recognizable cultural landmarks—the iconic Hollywood Walk of Fame© and the legendary Hollywood Sign©—preserving and promoting these global symbols on behalf of Hollywood and its residents, businesses, and visitors.

Ron Frierson serves as President and Chief Executive Officer, Dan Halden serves as Chief Operating Officer, and Jerry Neuman serves as Chair of the Board for the 2026–2027 term.

To learn more or become involved, visit www.hollywoodchamber.net.

Stephanie Kay Panabaker is an American actress, who was born on May 2, 1990 in Orange Grove, Texas, USA. She is the daughter of Donna (née Mayock) and Harold Panabaker. She has an older sister, [Danielle Panabaker](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1263939/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), who is also an actress. She started acting at various community theaters in Chicago, Philadelphia and Atlanta. In Naperville, Illinois, Kay attended Crone Middle School for sixth grade, and moved to Los Angeles, California, at the start of seventh grade. In between projects, Kay focuses on her academics. She graduated from high school, as valedictorian, when she was thirteen-years-old and received her Associate's Degree at age fifteen. Kay received two academic scholarships from Glendale Community College, where she attended, studying acting, and where she was on the Dean's list, graduating with honors. She was accepted to the UCLA online program as a junior history major, when she was fifteen, and completed her online BA in History from UCLA, before she turned eighteen. Kay was inspired by an elementary school teacher, who made learning exciting, and she wants to do the same for others, hoping to teach 4th or 5th grade, once she finishes her teaching degree. Panabaker has guest-starred in several television dramas and soap operas. She portrayed "Alice Brand" in [7th Heaven (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0115083/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); "Melissa Rue" in [ER (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0108757/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); "Sara" in [Port Charles (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0118435/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); "Carrie Bauer" in [The Brothers Garcia (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0235913/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); "Elisha" in [Medium (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0412175/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); "Lindsey Willows" in [CSI: Crime Scene Investigation (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0247082/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); to name a few. In film, she appeared in [Dead Heat (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0277744/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) as "Sam LaRoche"; and did some voice work in the Disney/Pixas film, [Monsters, Inc. (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0198781/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Panabaker's breakout role came when she starred in The WB's [Summerland (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0400037/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) as "Nikki Westerly", in the 2004-2005 season. She also appeared as "Georgie" in [Nancy Drew (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0479500/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), alongside [Emma Roberts](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0731075/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Amy Bruckner](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1426904/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). She starred in the 2007 movie, [Moondance Alexander (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0828065/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), along with actors, [Don Johnson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000467/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Lori Loughlin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0521753/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [James Best](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0078940/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Sasha Cohen](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1408846/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Whitney Sloan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1439209/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). She co-starred on the ABC sci-fi series, [No Ordinary Family (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1591493/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), along with actors [Michael Chiklis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004821/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Julie Benz](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004748/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Jimmy Bennett](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1497548/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Autumn Reeser](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1032208/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Romany Malco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0539082/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Stephen Collins](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004834/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).

**Annette Carol Bening** (born May 29, 1958) is an American actress. With a career spanning over four decades, she is known for [her versatile work across screen and stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Annette_Bening_performances "List of Annette Bening performances"). Bening has received [numerous accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Annette_Bening "List of awards and nominations received by Annette Bening"), including a [BAFTA Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Film_Awards "British Academy Film Awards"), two [Actor Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actor_Awards "Actor Awards"), and two [Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards"), in addition to nominations for five [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"), two [Tony Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Awards "Tony Awards"), and a [Primetime Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award "Primetime Emmy Award"), making her one of few artists nominated for the [Triple Crown of Acting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_Crown_of_Acting "Triple Crown of Acting") without winning.

A graduate of [San Francisco State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_State_University "San Francisco State University") and the [American Conservatory Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Conservatory_Theater "American Conservatory Theater"), Bening started her career on stage with the [Colorado Shakespeare Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Shakespeare_Festival "Colorado Shakespeare Festival") company in 1980, and played [Lady Macbeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Macbeth "Lady Macbeth") in 1984 at the [American Conservatory Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Conservatory_Theater "American Conservatory Theater"). She made her [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_(theatre) "Broadway (theatre)") debut in the [Tina Howe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tina_Howe "Tina Howe") play _[Coastal Disturbances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coastal\_Disturbances "Coastal Disturbances")_ (1987) for which she received a nomination for the [Tony Award for Best Featured Actress in a Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Featured_Actress_in_a_Play "Tony Award for Best Featured Actress in a Play"). Making her film debut in 1988, she gained further recognition for her role in _[The Grifters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Grifters\_(film) "The Grifters (film)")_ (1990), for which she received her first Academy Award nomination. This acclaim continued throughout the 1990s and 2000s with further Oscar-nominated performances in the comedy-dramas _[American Beauty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Beauty\_(1999\_film) "American Beauty (1999 film)")_ (1999) and _[Being Julia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Being\_Julia "Being Julia")_ (2004), which respectively won her the [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Leading_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actress in a Leading Role") and [Golden Globe for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_%E2%80%93_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy"). Bening's performance as the [title character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Title_character "Title character") in the British television film _[Mrs. Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mrs.\_Harris "Mrs. Harris")_ (2005) earned her a nomination for the [Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Miniseries or Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Lead_Actress_in_a_Limited_or_Anthology_Series_or_Movie "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie").

In following decades, Bening received two additional Oscar nominations for her leading roles as a [lesbian mother](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_parenting "Same-sex parenting") in _[The Kids Are All Right](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Kids\_Are\_All\_Right\_(film) "The Kids Are All Right (film)")_ (2010) and swimmer [Diana Nyad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diana_Nyad "Diana Nyad") in the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") biographical film _[Nyad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyad\_(film) "Nyad (film)")_ (2023), the former of which also won her a Golden Globe. She returned to Broadway in the revival of [Arthur Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Miller "Arthur Miller")'s _[All My Sons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All\_My\_Sons "All My Sons")_ (2019) earning another Tony nomination for [Best Actress in a Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Play "Tony Award for Best Actress in a Play"). Her other roles during this period include in the films _[20th Century Women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th\_Century\_Women "20th Century Women")_ (2016), _[Film Stars Don't Die in Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film\_Stars\_Don't\_Die\_in\_Liverpool "Film Stars Don't Die in Liverpool")_ (2017), _[Captain Marvel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain\_Marvel\_(film) "Captain Marvel (film)")_ (2019) and _[Death on the Nile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death\_on\_the\_Nile\_(2022\_film) "Death on the Nile (2022 film)")_ (2022), the miniseries _[Apples Never Fall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apples\_Never\_Fall "Apples Never Fall")_ (2024) and the series _[Dutton Ranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutton\_Ranch "Dutton Ranch")_ (2026).

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://www.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Annette_Bening&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Annette Carol Bening[[1]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-1) was born on May 29, 1958[[2]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-biography.com-2) in [Topeka, Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topeka,_Kansas "Topeka, Kansas"),[[2]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-biography.com-2) to Shirley Katherine (née Ashley)[[3]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-3) and Arnett Grant Bening. Her mother was a church singer and soloist, and her father was a sales training consultant and insurance salesman.[[4]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-5) Her parents, originally from [Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa "Iowa"), were practicing [Episcopalians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Episcopal_Church_in_the_United_States_of_America "Episcopal Church in the United States of America") and [conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatism_in_the_United_States "Conservatism in the United States")[Republicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"). She is of mostly German and English descent.[[6]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-ref12-6)[[7]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-7)

The youngest of four children, she has an older sister Jane, and two older brothers Bradley and Byron. The family moved to [Wichita, Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita,_Kansas "Wichita, Kansas"), in 1959, where she spent her early childhood. When Bening was in elementary school, her father relocated the family to [San Diego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego "San Diego"), California, where she spent the remainder of her youth.[[8]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-8)

She began acting in junior high school, playing the lead in _[The Sound of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sound\_of\_Music "The Sound of Music")_.[[9]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-9) She graduated in 1975 from San Diego's [Patrick Henry High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Henry_High_School_(San_Diego,_California) "Patrick Henry High School (San Diego, California)"), where she studied drama.[[10]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-11) She then spent a year working as a cook on a charter boat taking fishing parties out on the Pacific Ocean, and scuba diving for recreation. Bening attended [San Diego Mesa College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Mesa_College "San Diego Mesa College") and graduated with a degree in [Theatre Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatre_Arts "Theatre Arts") at [San Francisco State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_State_University "San Francisco State University").[[12]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-12)

## Career

[[edit](https://www.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Annette_Bening&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 1986–1999: Initial work, breakthrough and rise to prominence

[[edit](https://www.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Annette_Bening&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1986–1999: Initial work, breakthrough and rise to prominence")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/Annette_Bening_1999.jpg/250px-Annette_Bening_1999.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Annette_Bening_1999.jpg)

Bening in 1999

Bening began her career on stage with the [Colorado Shakespeare Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Shakespeare_Festival "Colorado Shakespeare Festival") company in 1980,[[13]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-13) and appeared in plays at the [San Diego Repertory Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Repertory_Theatre "San Diego Repertory Theatre"). She was a member of the acting company at the [American Conservatory Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Conservatory_Theater "American Conservatory Theater") in San Francisco while studying acting as part of the Advanced Theatre Training Program. There, she starred in such productions as Shakespeare's _[Macbeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macbeth "Macbeth")_ as [Lady Macbeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Macbeth "Lady Macbeth"). Bening also starred in productions of _[Pygmalion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pygmalion\_(play) "Pygmalion (play)")_ and _[The Cherry Orchard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cherry\_Orchard "The Cherry Orchard")_ at the [Denver Center Theatre Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Center_for_the_Performing_Arts "Denver Center for the Performing Arts") during the 1985–86 season. She made her [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") debut in 1987, garnering a [Tony Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award "Tony Award") nomination for [Best Featured Actress in a Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Featured_Actress_in_a_Play "Tony Award for Best Featured Actress in a Play")[[14]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-tony87-14) and receiving a [Theatre World Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatre_World_Award "Theatre World Award") for her performance as young photographer Holly Dancer in _[Coastal Disturbances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coastal\_Disturbances "Coastal Disturbances")_. Bening made her film debut in _[The Great Outdoors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Great\_Outdoors\_(film) "The Great Outdoors (film)")_ (1988), starring [Dan Aykroyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Aykroyd "Dan Aykroyd") and [John Candy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Candy "John Candy"). Her next role was as the Marquise de Merteuil in _[Valmont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valmont\_(film) "Valmont (film)")_ (1989) opposite [Colin Firth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Firth "Colin Firth").

Bening achieved her breakthrough with her performance as [con artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Con_artist "Con artist") Myra Langtry in the neo-noir crime thriller _[The Grifters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Grifters\_(film) "The Grifters (film)")_ (1990), for which she earned her first nominations for the [Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress") and the [BAFTA Award for Best Actress in a Supporting Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Supporting_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actress in a Supporting Role").[[15]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-Oscar63-15) In 1991, she portrayed [Virginia Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Hill "Virginia Hill") in [Barry Levinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Levinson "Barry Levinson")'s biopic _[Bugsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bugsy "Bugsy")_, alongside [Warren Beatty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Beatty "Warren Beatty"). For _Bugsy_, she received her first nomination for the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_%E2%80%93_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama"). Bening co-starred with [Harrison Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford "Harrison Ford") in _[Regarding Henry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regarding\_Henry "Regarding Henry")_. In 1994, Bening and Beatty starred together again, in _[Love Affair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_Affair\_(1994\_film) "Love Affair (1994 film)")_. In 1995, Bening played a leading role as an environmental [lobbyist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lobbyist "Lobbyist") in _[The American President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_American\_President "The American President")_ with [Michael Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Douglas "Michael Douglas"), a role she followed with [Tim Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Burton "Tim Burton")'s sci-fi spoof _[Mars Attacks!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_Attacks! "Mars Attacks!")_ (1996), and _[The Siege](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Siege\_(1998\_film) "The Siege (1998 film)")_ (1998), a thriller with [Denzel Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denzel_Washington "Denzel Washington") and [Bruce Willis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Willis "Bruce Willis").

Bening garnered acclaim for her starring role in [Sam Mendes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Mendes "Sam Mendes")' directorial debut film, _[American Beauty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Beauty\_(1999\_film) "American Beauty (1999 film)")_ (1999). She starred opposite [Kevin Spacey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Spacey "Kevin Spacey") in the dark comedy-drama about a man suffering a mid-life crisis in 90s American suburbia. The film won five [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"), including [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"). For her performance as Carolyn Burnham, a materialistic wife engaging in an affair, Bening won the [BAFTA Award for Best Actress in a Leading Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Leading_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actress in a Leading Role") and the [Actor Award for Outstanding Performance by a Female Actor in a Leading Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actor_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_a_Female_Actor_in_a_Leading_Role "Actor Award for Outstanding Performance by a Female Actor in a Leading Role"), in addition to her first nomination for the [Academy Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actress "Academy Award for Best Actress")[[16]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-Oscar72-16) and her second nomination for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama.[[17]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-globes-17)

In 1999, Bening returned to the stage for the first time in 10 years playing the title role in _[Hedda Gabler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedda\_Gabler "Hedda Gabler")_ at the [Geffen Playhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geffen_Playhouse "Geffen Playhouse") in Los Angeles. The _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ praised her performance saying "Bening uses her vocal instrument to fine effect, without throwing it around... In the movies you don't always hear what Bening can do with that voice, especially when she's playing virtuous, "sensible" types... But Ibsen's antiheroine—thwarted sensualist, a woman wrestling with her inner troll, belle of a ball that never comes—is neither virtuous nor sensible. She's no easy-to-read villain, either, nor a mere vindictive brat, though plenty of actresses have reduced her thus. Bening lays into the venomous sarcasm mighty heavily, but she's cagey enough to avoid reductive extremes."[[18]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-18)

### 2000–2014: Established actress

[[edit](https://www.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Annette_Bening&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2000–2014: Established actress")]

Bening starred in other films, including _[In Dreams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In\_Dreams\_(film) "In Dreams (film)")_ (1999) and _[What Planet Are You From?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What\_Planet\_Are\_You\_From%3F "What Planet Are You From?")_ (2000). Bening played Sue Barlow in _[Open Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open\_Range\_(2003\_film) "Open Range (2003 film)")_ (2003). She earned critical acclaim for playing the eponymous lead in the comedy-drama _[Being Julia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Being\_Julia "Being Julia")_ (2004). For her performance in the film, she won her first [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture_Comedy_or_Musical "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress – Motion Picture Comedy or Musical") in addition to her second [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actress "Academy Award for Best Actress") and [Actor Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actor_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_a_Female_Actor_in_a_Leading_Role "Actor Award for Outstanding Performance by a Female Actor in a Leading Role") nominations.[[19]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-Oscar77-19) She received [Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Lead_Actress_in_a_Limited_or_Anthology_Series_or_Movie "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie") and [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_%E2%80%93_Miniseries_or_Television_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress – Miniseries or Television Film") nominations for her role of convicted celebrity murderer [Jean Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Harris "Jean Harris") in the [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") film _[Mrs. Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mrs.\_Harris "Mrs. Harris")_ (2005).[[20]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-emmy-20) She replaced [Julianne Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julianne_Moore "Julianne Moore") and starred as Deirdre Burroughs, an aspiring poet with [bipolar disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bipolar_disorder "Bipolar disorder"), in the film adaptation of _[Running with Scissors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running\_with\_Scissors\_(film) "Running with Scissors (film)")_ (2006).

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/Mrs._Harris_001_%287271521236%29.jpg/250px-Mrs._Harris_001_%287271521236%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mrs._Harris_001_(7271521236).jpg)

Bening at the Toronto Film Festival 2005

. She earned her fifth [Golden Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_%E2%80%93_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy") nomination.[[17]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-globes-17) Bening starred in _[The Women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Women\_(2008\_film) "The Women (2008 film)")_ (2008) remake. In 2009, Bening starred in a new interpretation of the [Euripides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euripides "Euripides") classic _[Medea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medea\_(play) "Medea (play)")_ at [UCLA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCLA "UCLA")'s Freud Playhouse.[[21]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-21) She received positive reviews for her performance in the independent film _[Mother and Child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mother\_and\_Child\_(2009\_film) "Mother and Child (2009 film)")_ (2009).[[22]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-22)

In 2010, she starred in [_The Female of the Species_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Female_of_the_Species_(play) "The Female of the Species (play)"), [Joanna Murray-Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joanna_Murray-Smith "Joanna Murray-Smith")'s comedy, at the [Geffen Playhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geffen_Playhouse "Geffen Playhouse") in Los Angeles.[[23]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-23) Later that year, Bening received critical acclaim for her performance in _[The Kids Are All Right](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Kids\_Are\_All\_Right\_(film) "The Kids Are All Right (film)")_; a reviewer said that she "deserves an Oscar" and another praised her "sublime" performance.[[24]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-24) For her role, Bening won her second [Golden Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_%E2%80%93_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy") and was nominated for her third Academy Award, third BAFTA, and six and seventh [Actor Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actor_Awards "Actor Awards") (she received nominations for both [Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actor_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_a_Female_Actor_in_a_Leading_Role "Actor Award for Outstanding Performance by a Female Actor in a Leading Role") and [Best Cast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actor_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_a_Cast_in_a_Motion_Picture "Actor Award for Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture")).[[17]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-globes-17)[[25]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-Oscar83-25)

In 2012, Bening's audiobook recording of [Virginia Woolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Woolf "Virginia Woolf")'s _[Mrs. Dalloway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mrs.\_Dalloway "Mrs. Dalloway")_ was released at [Audible.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audible.com "Audible.com"). In 2014, she starred in Shakespeare's _[King Lear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_Lear "King Lear")_ at the [Delacorte Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delacorte_Theater "Delacorte Theater") in [Central Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park "Central Park"), as part of the Public Theatre's Free [Shakespeare in the Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Shakespeare_Festival "New York Shakespeare Festival"). It marked her first New York stage appearance in twenty years.[[26]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-27) Bening starred in [Dan Fogelman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Fogelman "Dan Fogelman")'s 2015 American [comedy drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_drama "Comedy drama")[_Danny Collins_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Collins_(film) "Danny Collins (film)") with [Al Pacino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Pacino "Al Pacino").

### 2016–present: Later career

[[edit](https://www.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Annette_Bening&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2016–present: Later career")]

In 2016, Bening starred in [Mike Mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Mills_(director) "Mike Mills (director)")'s comedy drama _[20th Century Women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th\_Century\_Women "20th Century Women")_ alongside [Elle Fanning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elle_Fanning "Elle Fanning"), [Greta Gerwig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Gerwig "Greta Gerwig"), and [Billy Crudup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Crudup "Billy Crudup").[[28]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-28) Bening played a chain-smoking first-wave feminist struggling to raise her teenage son. Sheila O'Malley of _[Roger Ebert.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger\_Ebert "Roger Ebert")_ declared, "Bening has one of the best performances of the year (and one of Bening's personal best as well)".[[29]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-29) For her performance, she was nominated for the [Independent Spirit Award for Best Female Lead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_Spirit_Award_for_Best_Female_Lead "Independent Spirit Award for Best Female Lead") and the [Critics' Choice Movie Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critics'_Choice_Movie_Award_for_Best_Actress "Critics' Choice Movie Award for Best Actress").

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Life_Itself_cast_at_TIFF_2018.jpg/250px-Life_Itself_cast_at_TIFF_2018.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Life_Itself_cast_at_TIFF_2018.jpg)

[Olivia Wilde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Wilde "Olivia Wilde"), Bening, [Mandy Patinkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandy_Patinkin "Mandy Patinkin"), [Olivia Cooke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Cooke "Olivia Cooke"), [Laia Costa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laia_Costa "Laia Costa") at the [TIFF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_International_Film_Festival "Toronto International Film Festival") premiere for _[Life Itself](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life\_Itself\_(2018\_film) "Life Itself (2018 film)")_ in 2018

The following year, she portrayed [Gloria Grahame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloria_Grahame "Gloria Grahame") in _[Film Stars Don't Die in Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film\_Stars\_Don't\_Die\_in\_Liverpool "Film Stars Don't Die in Liverpool")_ (2017) alongside [Jamie Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Bell "Jamie Bell"), [Vanessa Redgrave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Redgrave "Vanessa Redgrave"), and [Julie Walters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julie_Walters "Julie Walters"). [Peter Bradshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Bradshaw "Peter Bradshaw") critic from _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ praised her performance declaring, "Bening is excellent as Grahame: imperious, vulnerable, romantic, sexually excited about her younger man, wanly aware of secrets she cannot share with him".[[30]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-30) She received her third nomination for the BAFTA Award for Best Actress in a Leading Role for her performance in the film. The following year, she starred as Irina Arkadina in _[The Seagull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Seagull\_(2018\_film) "The Seagull (2018 film)")_ and as Dr. Cait Morris in _[Life Itself](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life\_Itself\_(2018\_film) "Life Itself (2018 film)")_ (2018).

In 2019, Bening returned to the [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") stage after a 32-year absence, starring in the revival of [Arthur Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Miller "Arthur Miller")'s _[All My Sons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All\_My\_Sons "All My Sons")_ alongside [Tracy Letts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracy_Letts "Tracy Letts") at the [Roundabout Theatre Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roundabout_Theatre_Company "Roundabout Theatre Company")'s [American Airlines Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Airlines_Theatre "American Airlines Theatre"). The play opened on April 4, 2019, and closed on June 23, 2019.[[31]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-31) She was nominated for the [Tony Award for Best Actress in a Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Play "Tony Award for Best Actress in a Play") for her performance.[[32]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-tony19-32) The following year, she portrayed Senator [Dianne Feinstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dianne_Feinstein "Dianne Feinstein") in the political drama film _[The Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Report\_(2019\_film) "The Report (2019 film)")_ (2019) for which she earned her first nomination for the [Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actress – Motion Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture "Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actress – Motion Picture").[[17]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-globes-17)

Bening joined the [Marvel Cinematic Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe "Marvel Cinematic Universe") playing Dr. Wendy Lawson in _[Captain Marvel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain\_Marvel\_(film) "Captain Marvel (film)")_ (2019) alongside [Brie Larson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brie_Larson "Brie Larson"). The film was a massive financial box-office hit. In 2022, she acted in [Kenneth Branagh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Branagh "Kenneth Branagh")'s _[Death on the Nile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death\_on\_the\_Nile\_(2022\_film) "Death on the Nile (2022 film)")_ and the comedy _[Jerry & Marge Go Large](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry\_&\_Marge\_Go\_Large "Jerry & Marge Go Large")_ opposite [Bryan Cranston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Cranston "Bryan Cranston"). That same year, she filmed _[Nyad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyad\_(film) "Nyad (film)")_ alongside [Jodie Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Foster "Jodie Foster"), where Bening portrayed [long-distance swimmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_swimming "Long-distance swimming")[Diana Nyad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diana_Nyad "Diana Nyad"). The film was distributed by [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") and premiered at the [2023 Toronto International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Toronto_International_Film_Festival "2023 Toronto International Film Festival").[[33]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-33) Her performance earned high critical acclaim,[[34]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-36) and earned her a fifth [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actress "Academy Award for Best Actress") nomination.[[37]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-Oscar96-37)

In 2023, Bening was elected Chair of the Board of Trustees for the [Entertainment Community Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_Community_Fund "Entertainment Community Fund").[[38]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-38) She next starred in [Liane Moriarty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liane_Moriarty "Liane Moriarty")'s _[Apples Never Fall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apples\_Never\_Fall "Apples Never Fall")_, based on the bestselling thriller which was adapted by [Peacock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_(streaming_service) "Peacock (streaming service)") and also features [Sam Neill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Neill "Sam Neill"). The limited series premiered with all episodes immediately available to stream on March 15, 2024.

## Personal life
