Bening has received numerous accolades, including a [BAFTA Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Film_Awards "British Academy Film Awards"),[[42]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-42) two [Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards"),[[17]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-globes-17) and two [Actor Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actor_Awards "Actor Awards").[[43]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-43) She has also received nominations for a [Primetime Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award "Primetime Emmy Award")[[20]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-emmy-20) and two [Tony Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award "Tony Award").[[14]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-tony87-14)[[32]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-tony19-32)

She has also received five [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") nominations, for the following films:

*   [63rd Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/63rd_Academy_Awards "63rd Academy Awards"): [Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress") nomination for _[The Grifters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Grifters\_(film) "The Grifters (film)")_ (1990)[[15]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-Oscar63-15)
*   [72nd Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/72nd_Academy_Awards "72nd Academy Awards"): [Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actress "Academy Award for Best Actress") nomination for _[American Beauty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Beauty\_(1999\_film) "American Beauty (1999 film)")_ (1999)[[16]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-Oscar72-16)
*   [77th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/77th_Academy_Awards "77th Academy Awards"): Best Actress nomination for _[Being Julia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Being\_Julia "Being Julia")_ (2004)[[19]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-Oscar77-19)
*   [83rd Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/83rd_Academy_Awards "83rd Academy Awards"): Best Actress nomination for _[The Kids Are All Right](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Kids\_Are\_All\_Right\_(film) "The Kids Are All Right (film)")_ (2010)[[25]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-Oscar83-25)
*   [96th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/96th_Academy_Awards "96th Academy Awards"), Best Actress nomination for _[Nyad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyad\_(film) "Nyad (film)")_ (2023)[[37]](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_Bening#cite_note-Oscar96-37)

[](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0405103/bio/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_sm)

Sarah Hyland was born in New York City to actors [Melissa D. Canaday](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4420107/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Edward James Hyland](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0405079/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). She began in the business at the age of 4 with commercial work and voice overs. Her first film was [Private Parts (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119951/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). She then moved on to [The Object of My Affection (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120772/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and then spent time on [Another World (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057731/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) as "Rain Wolfe", a child found in the park, and fostered by Josie and Gary. Sarah would go on to work with [Amy Carlson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0137856/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) ("Josie" on AW) several more times: [Falcone (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0233052/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Law & Order (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0098844/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Law & Order: Trial by Jury (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0406429/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Sarah was cast as one of the young "Audrey Hepburns" in [Jennifer Love Hewitt](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001349/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s [The Audrey Hepburn Story (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0163887/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) the same year she was cast as "Molly" in ABC's [Annie (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0207972/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) starring [Kathy Bates](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000870/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Audra McDonald](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0567653/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Alan Cumming](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001086/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Victor Garber](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001255/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Kristin Chenoweth](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0155693/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Joe Gould's Secret (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0172632/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Falcone (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0233052/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Aside from all of her film and television work, Sarah studied voice, ballet, jazz, hip-hop, tap, Theatre Dance, and performed with her tap and Theatre dance class at "Reel to Real" at Lincoln Center as invited performers.  
  
A New York-born and raised girl, Sarah spent much of her time working in film, television, and voicing many radio ads, as well as traveling with her father, [Edward James Hyland](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0405079/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), while he worked at many different theaters in the country. She was home schooled by her mother until 2nd grade and then attended Public School. In 6th Grade, she was accepted into PPAS (Professional Performing Arts School) where she stayed until she graduated in 2008. When Sarah turned 18, she moved to Los Angeles, CA and, within two weeks, had landed a pilot named "My American Family". Once picked up the name was changed to [Modern Family (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1442437/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). To date, Sarah portrays "Haley Dunphy", the eldest Dunphy child. [Modern Family (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1442437/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) has won multiple awards most notably the Emmy for Outstanding Comedy Series.  
  
Before moving to L.A., Sarah did a multitude of film and television and, at the age of 11 1/2, she made her stage debut at Papermill Playhouse in Millburn, NJ in the title role of "Annie". From there, Sarah added many more stage productions to her resume including "Bad Girls", "Dark Part of the Forest" and both productions on and off Broadway of "Grey Gardens" in the role of "Jackie Bouvier". "Grey Gardens" was nominated for Best Musical at the Tony Awards, and [Christine Ebersole](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002056/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Mary Louise Wilson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0933840/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) won Best Actress and Best Supporting Actress Tony's for their work. [William Ivey Long](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0519235/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) won for his costume design. Sarah also did many development workshops including: "A Little Princess", "Bye Bye Birdie', and "Shrek, the Musical", to name a few. Sarah has worked with some of the top talent in the Industry: [Tim Robbins](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000209/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Stanley Tucci](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001804/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Ian Holmes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0992533/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Steve Martin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000188/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [John Turturro](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001806/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Hope Davis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0204706/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Keir Dullea](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001158/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Frances Fisher](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004920/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Brooke Shields](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000222/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Kim Raver](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005339/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Lindsay Price](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0697010/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Timothy Busfield](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0124079/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), among so many other incredible talents. She has guest starred on [Touched by an Angel (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0108968/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Law & Order: Trial by Jury (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0406429/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and twice on [Law & Order: Special Victims Unit (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0203259/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Her second turn on [Hothouse (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1248624/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) gave her a breakthrough role where she portrayed "Jennifer Banks", a student at a school for the gifted who kills her roommate in a drug fueled rage.  
  
Her work on [Lipstick Jungle (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0489606/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) as [Brooke Shields](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000222/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s daughter further showcased her talent and, because of LJ's cancellation, drew her to Los Angeles and the role of "Haley Dunphy" on [Modern Family (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1442437/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).  
  
Sarah has a maltipoo named Barkley, and is happily living in the Los Angeles Area. She is the Face of "Wallflower Jeans". Sarah's brother, [Ian Donovan Hyland](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1530860/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), is also an actor and, even though most think Ian is her older brother, he is really 4 years her junior. Her father is a stage and film actor based in New York, and her mother is an acting coach to young actors.

*   [Trivia](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0405103/trivia/?ref_=nm_dyk_trv)Diagnosed with kidney dysplasia at age nine; her kidneys did not develop properly when she was in the womb and frequently form painful cysts. She required a kidney transplant in April 2012. Her father donated his kidney, but in October 2016 her body started to reject it. She underwent different tests and treatments to try to save the kidney but none of the treatments worked. She started regularly undergoing dialysis, which led to severe weight loss. Doctors removed the transplanted kidney in May 2017, and her younger brother Ian offered his kidney, which was a match. However, she felt depressed about her health issues and contemplated suicide. In September 2017 she underwent a second kidney transplant, but her health problems didn't end there; she also has endometriosis, and the pain was becoming unbearable. In addition, she had a previously undiagnosed abdominal hernia. That led to more surgeries. she has had six in 16 months, and 16 total over the course of her life, including laparoscopic surgery for the endometriosis and a hernia repair surgery. Stephanie Kay Panabaker is an American actress, who was born on May 2, 1990 in Orange Grove, Texas, USA. She is the daughter of Donna (née Mayock) and Harold Panabaker. She has an older sister, [Danielle Panabaker](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1263939/?ls), who is also an actress. She started acting at various community theaters in Chicago, Philadelphia and Atlanta. In Naperville, Illinois, Kay attended Crone Middle School for sixth grade, and moved to Los Angeles, California, at the start of seventh grade. In between projects, Kay focuses on her academics. She graduated from high school, as valedictorian, when she was thirteen-years-old and received her Associate's Degree at age fifteen. Kay received two academic scholarships from Glendale Community College, where she attended, studying acting, and where she was on the Dean's list, graduating with honors. She was accepted to the UCLA online program as a junior history major, when she was fifteen, and completed her online BA in History from UCLA, before she turned eighteen. Kay was inspired by an elementary school teacher, who made learning exciting, and she wants to do the same for others, hoping to teach 4th or 5th grade, once she finishes her teaching degree. Panabaker has guest-starred in several television dramas and soap operas. She portrayed "Alice Brand" in [7th Heaven (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0115083/?ls); "Melissa Rue" in [ER (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0108757/?ls); "Sara" in [Port Charles (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0118435/?ls); "Carrie Bauer" in [The Brothers Garcia (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0235913/?ls); "Elisha" in [Medium (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0412175/?ls); "Lindsey Willows" in [CSI: Crime Scene Investigation (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0247082/?ls); to name a few. In film, she appeared in [Dead Heat (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0277744/?ls) as "Sam LaRoche"; and did some voice work in the Disney/Pixas film, [Monsters, Inc. (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0198781/?ls). Panabaker's breakout role came when she starred in The WB's [Summerland (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0400037/?ls) as "Nikki Westerly", in the 2004-2005 season. She also appeared as "Georgie" in [Nancy Drew (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0479500/?ls), alongside [Emma Roberts](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0731075/?ls) and [Amy Bruckner](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1426904/?ls). She starred in the 2007 movie, [Moondance Alexander (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0828065/?ls), along with actors, [Don Johnson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000467/?ls), [Lori Loughlin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0521753/?ls), [James Best](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0078940/?ls), [Sasha Cohen](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1408846/?ls) and [Whitney Sloan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1439209/?ls).  #### [3. Sarah Hyland](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0405103/?ref_=ls_t_3)

Sarah Hyland was born in New York City to actors [Melissa D. Canaday](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4420107/?ls) and [Edward James Hyland](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0405079/?ls). She began in the business at the age of 4 with commercial work and voice overs. Her first film was [Private Parts (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119951/?ls). She then moved on to [The Object of My Affection (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120772/?ls) and then spent time on [Another World (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057731/?ls) as "Rain Wolfe", a child found in the park, and fostered by Josie and Gary. Sarah would go on to work with [Amy Carlson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0137856/?ls) ("Josie" on AW) several more times: [Falcone (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0233052/?ls), [Law & Order (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0098844/?ls) and [Law & Order: Trial by Jury (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0406429/?ls). Sarah was cast as one of the young "Audrey Hepburns" in [Jennifer Love Hewitt](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001349/?ls)'s [The Audrey Hepburn Story (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0163887/?ls) the same year she was cast as "Molly" in ABC's [Annie (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0207972/?ls) starring [Kathy Bates](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000870/?ls), [Audra McDonald](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0567653/?ls), [Alan Cumming](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001086/?ls), [Victor Garber](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001255/?ls) and [Kristin Chenoweth](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0155693/?ls), [Joe Gould's Secret (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0172632/?ls) and [Falcone (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0233052/?ls). Aside from all of her film and television work, Sarah studied voice, ballet, jazz, hip-hop, tap, Theatre Dance, and performed with her tap and Theatre dance class at "Reel to Real" at Lincoln Center as invited performers.  
  
A New York-born and raised girl, Sarah spent much of her time working in film, television, and voicing many radio ads, as well as traveling with her father, [Edward James Hyland](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0405079/?ls), while he worked at many different theaters in the country. She was home schooled by her mother until 2nd grade and then attended Public School. In 6th Grade, she was accepted into PPAS (Professional Performing Arts School) where she stayed until she graduated in 2008. When Sarah turned 18, she moved to Los Angeles, CA and, within two weeks, had landed a pilot named "My American Family". Once picked up the name was changed to [Modern Family (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1442437/?ls). To date, Sarah portrays "Haley Dunphy", the eldest Dunphy child. [Modern Family (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1442437/?ls) has won multiple awards most notably the Emmy for Outstanding Comedy Series.  
  
Before moving to L.A., Sarah did a multitude of film and television and, at the age of 11 1/2, she made her stage debut at Papermill Playhouse in Millburn, NJ in the title role of "Annie". From there, Sarah added many more stage productions to her resume including "Bad Girls", "Dark Part of the Forest" and both productions on and off Broadway of "Grey Gardens" in the role of "Jackie Bouvier". "Grey Gardens" was nominated for Best Musical at the Tony Awards, and [Christine Ebersole](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002056/?ls) and [Mary Louise Wilson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0933840/?ls) won Best Actress and Best Supporting Actress Tony's for their work. [William Ivey Long](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0519235/?ls) won for his costume design. Sarah also did many development workshops including: "A Little Princess", "Bye Bye Birdie', and "Shrek, the Musical", to name a few. Sarah has worked with some of the top talent in the Industry: [Tim Robbins](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000209/?ls), [Stanley Tucci](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001804/?ls), [Ian Holmes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0992533/?ls), [Steve Martin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000188/?ls), [John Turturro](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001806/?ls), [Hope Davis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0204706/?ls), [Keir Dullea](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001158/?ls), [Frances Fisher](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004920/?ls), [Brooke Shields](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000222/?ls), [Kim Raver](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005339/?ls), [Lindsay Price](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0697010/?ls), [Timothy Busfield](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0124079/?ls), among so many other incredible talents. She has guest starred on [Touched by an Angel (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0108968/?ls), [Law & Order: Trial by Jury (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0406429/?ls) and twice on [Law & Order: Special Victims Unit (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0203259/?ls). Her second turn on [Hothouse (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1248624/?ls) gave her a breakthrough role where she portrayed "Jennifer Banks", a student at a school for the gifted who kills her roommate in a drug fueled rage.  
  
Her work on [Lipstick Jungle (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0489606/?ls) as [Brooke Shields](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000222/?ls)'s daughter further showcased her talent and, because of LJ's cancellation, drew her to Los Angeles and the role of "Haley Dunphy" on [Modern Family (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1442437/?ls).  
  
Sarah has a maltipoo named Barkley, and is happily living in the Los Angeles Area. She is the Face of "Wallflower Jeans". Sarah's brother, [Ian Donovan Hyland](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1530860/?ls), is also an actor and, even though most think Ian is her older brother, he is really 4 years her junior. Her father is a stage and film actor based in New York, and her mother is an acting coach to young actors.

 #### [4. Emma Watson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0914612/?ref_=ls_t_4) 

    *   Actress
    *   Director

[The Perks of Being a Wallflower (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1659337/?ref_=ls_knf_4)

Emma Charlotte Duerre Watson was born in Paris, France, to British parents, Jacqueline Luesby and Chris Watson, both lawyers. She moved to Oxfordshire when she was five, where she attended the Dragon School. From the age of six, Emma knew that she wanted to be an actress and, for a number of years, she trained at the Oxford branch of Stagecoach Theatre Arts, a part-time theatre school where she studied singing, dancing and acting. By the age of ten, she had performed and taken the lead in various Stagecoach productions and school plays.  
  
In 1999, casting began for [Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0241527/?ls) , the film adaptation of British author J.K. Rowling's bestselling novel. Casting agents found Emma through her Oxford theatre teacher. After eight consistent auditions, producer David Heyman told Emma and fellow applicants, [Daniel Radcliffe](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0705356/?ls) and [Rupert Grint](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0342488/?ls), that they had been cast for the roles of the three leads, Hermione Granger, Harry Potter and Ron Weasley. The release of [Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0241527/?ls) was Emma's cinematic screen debut. The film broke records for opening-day sales and opening-weekend takings and was the highest-grossing film of 2001. Critics praised the film and the performances of the three leading young actors. The highly distributed British newspaper, 'The Daily Telegraph', called her performance "admirable". Later, Emma was nominated for five awards for her performance in the film, winning the Young Artist Award for Leading Young Actress in a Feature Film.  
  
After the release of the first film of the highly successful franchise, Emma became one of the most well-known actresses in the world. She continued to play the role of Hermione Granger for nearly ten years, in all of the following Harry Potter films: [Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0241527/?ls) , [Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0295297/?ls), [Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0304141/?ls), [Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0330373/?ls), [Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0373889/?ls), [Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0417741/?ls), [Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 1 (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0926084/?ls), and [Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 2 (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1201607/?ls). Emma acquired two Critics' Choice Award nominations from the Broadcast Film Critics Association for her work in Harry Potter And The Prisoner Of Azkaban and Harry Potter And The Goblet Of Fire. The completion of the seventh and eight movies saw Emma receive nominations in 2011 for a Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Award, and for Best Actress at the Jameson Empire Awards. The Harry Potter franchise won the BAFTA for Outstanding British Contribution to Cinema in February 2011.  
  
2011 saw Emma in Simon Curtis's [My Week with Marilyn (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1655420/?ls), alongside a stellar cast of Oscar nominees including Michelle Williams as Marilyn Monroe and Kenneth Branagh as Sir Laurence Olivier, in addition to Eddie Redmayne, Dame Judi Dench, Dougray Scott, Zoe Wanamaker, Toby Jones and Dominic Cooper. Chronicling a week in [Marilyn Monroe](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000054/?ls)'s life, the film featured Emma in the supporting role of Lucy, a costume assistant to Colin Clark (Redmayne). The film was released by The Weinstein Company and was nominated for a Golden Globe for Best Motion Picture - Comedy or Musical. In 2012 Emma was seen in Stephen Chbosky's adaptation of his coming-of-age novel [The Perks of Being a Wallflower (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1659337/?ls), starring opposite [Logan Lerman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0503567/?ls) and [Ezra Miller](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3009232/?ls). This independent drama centered around Charlie (Lerman), an introverted freshman who is taken under the wings of two seniors (Watson and Miller) who welcome him to the real world. The film premiered at the 2012 Toronto International Film Festival and received rave reviews. The film won the People's Choice Award for Favourite Dramatic Movie and Emma also picked up the People's Choice Award for Favourite Dramatic Movie Actress. Emma was awarded a second time for this role with the Best Supporting Actress Award at the San Diego Film Critics Society Awards where the film also won the Best Ensemble Performance Award.  
  
In summer 2013, Emma starred in [Sofia Coppola](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001068/?ls)'s American satirical black comedy crime film, [The Bling Ring (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2132285/?ls), opposite [Katie Chang](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4583512/?ls) and [Israel Broussard](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3441152/?ls). The film took inspiration from real events and followed a group of teenagers who, obsessed with fashion and fame, burgled the homes of celebrities in Los Angeles. The film opened the Un Certain Regard section of the 2013 Cannes Film Festival. Emma also appeared in a cameo role as herself in Seth Rogen's apocalypse comedy This Is The End (2013). The film tells the story about what happens to some of Hollywood's best loved celebrities when the apocalypse strikes during a party at James Franco's house.  
  
In 2014, Emma was seen in Darren Aronofsky's [Noah (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1959490/?ls), opposite [Russell Crowe](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000128/?ls), [Jennifer Connelly](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000124/?ls), [Ray Winstone](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0935653/?ls), [Douglas Booth](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3150488/?ls), [Logan Lerman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0503567/?ls), and [Anthony Hopkins](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000164/?ls). The film told the epic, biblical tale of Noah and the ark. Emma plays the role of Ila, a young woman who develops a close relationship with Noah's son, Shem (Booth). Noah made an outstanding $300m since its release in March. In 2015, Emma starred in [Regression (2015)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3319920/?ls), written Crowley Baruc, and directed by Alejandro Amenábar. Also headlined by Oscar-nominated Ethan Hawke, and set in Minnesota in 1990, Regression tells the story of Detective Bruce Kenner (Hawke), who investigates the case of young Angela, played by Emma, who accuses her father of sexual abuse.  
  
In 2012, Emma was honored with the Calvin Klein Emerging Star Award at the ELLE Women in Hollywood Awards. In 2013, Emma was awarded the Trailblazer Award at the MTV Movie Awards in April and was honored with the GQ Woman of the Year Award at the GQ Awards in September. Further to her acting career, Emma is a Goodwill Ambassador for the UN, promoting gender equality and the empowerment of women. Emma graduated from Brown University in May 2014.  
  
In 2017, Emma starred in the live-action Disney fantasy [Beauty and the Beast (2017)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2771200/?ls), one of the biggest movies of all time in the U.S., and the dramatic thriller [The Circle (2017)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt4287320/?ls).

[The Twilight Saga: Eclipse (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1325004/?ref_=ls_knf_5)

Though most famous for her role as Isabella "Bella" Swan in The [Twilight (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1099212/?ls) Saga, Kristen Stewart has been a working actor since her early years in Los Angeles, California. Her parents, [John Stewart](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0829522/?ls) and [Jules Stewart](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0543032/?ls), both work in film and television. The family includes three boys, Stewart's older brother [Cameron Stewart](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2452920/?ls) and two adopted brothers Dana and Taylor.  
  
After a talent scout caught her grade school performance in a play at the age of eight, she appeared on television in a few small roles. Her first significant role came when she was cast as Sam Jennings in [The Safety of Objects (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0256359/?ls). Soon after that, she starred alongside [Jodie Foster](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000149/?ls) in the hit drama, [Panic Room (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0258000/?ls) and was nominated for a Young Artist Award.  
  
Praised for her Panic Room performance, she went on to join the cast of [Cold Creek Manor (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0331468/?ls) as the daughter of [Dennis Quaid](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000598/?ls) and [Sharon Stone](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000232/?ls). Though the film did not do well at the box office, she received another nomination for a Young Artist Award. After appearing in a handful of movies and a Showtime movie called [Speak (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0378793/?ls), Stewart was cast in the role of a teenage singer living in a commune in [Sean Penn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000576/?ls)'s [Into the Wild (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0758758/?ls), a critically acclaimed biopic. A third Young Artist Award nomination resulted in a win for this role. She also appeared in [Mary Stuart Masterson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000524/?ls)'s [The Cake Eaters (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0418586/?ls) that same year.  
  
Just 17, Stewart took on the starring role in [Twilight (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1099212/?ls) which was based on a series of the same name written by [Stephenie Meyer](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2769412/?ls), the novel already had a huge following and the film opened to fans anxious to see the vampire romance brought to life. Awarded the MTV Movie Award for Best Female Performance, Stewart's turn as Bella continued in the sequels [The Twilight Saga: New Moon (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1259571/?ls) and [The Twilight Saga: Eclipse (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1325004/?ls). The final installments of the series started filming in late 2010, and were released the following years, as [The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 1 (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1324999/?ls) and [The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 2 (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1673434/?ls).  
  
Despite her stratospheric launch into stardom with the Twilight films, she stayed true to her roots by working on a number of indie projects, including [Adventureland (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1091722/?ls) (filmed prior to the Twilight series) and [Welcome to the Rileys (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1183923/?ls). And she took on the daunting task of playing hard rocker [Joan Jett](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005053/?ls) in [Floria Sigismondi](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0797455/?ls)'s [The Runaways (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1017451/?ls) alongside [Dakota Fanning](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0266824/?ls). Stewart received praise for her acting and musical performances and later won the 2010 BAFTA Rising Star Award and best actress at the Milan International Film Festival for [Welcome to the Rileys (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1183923/?ls).  
  
Stewart worked on several other leading roles between the Twilight Saga installments including the #1 summer box office hit, [Snow White and the Huntsman (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1735898/?ls), and the Cannes selection [On the Road (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0337692/?ls). She also performed in the Sundance drama [Camp X-Ray (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2994190/?ls), Cannes selection [Clouds of Sils Maria (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2452254/?ls), for which she won a César Award, and the Lionsgate action comedy, [American Ultra (2015)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3316948/?ls), also starring Jesse Eisenberg, the Adventureland duo. She also delivered an acclaimed turn opposite Academy Award-winner Julianne Moore in [Still Alice (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3316960/?ls). For the remainder of the decade, Kristen alternated choice supporting roles, such as [Billy Lynn's Long Halftime Walk (2016)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2513074/?ls) and [Café Society (2016)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt4513674/?ls), with starring roles in films about historical figures, including [Lizzie (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt5160938/?ls) and [Seberg (2019)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1780967/?ls), and special effects/action thrillers [Charlie's Angels (2019)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt5033998/?ls) and [Underwater (2020)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt5774060/?ls).  
  
Kristen had a change-of-pace role in the romantic comedy [Happiest Season (2020)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8522006/?ls), about an LGBT+ couple, and received universal acclaim, and her first Oscar nomination, for Best Actress, for her performance as [Princess Diana](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0697740/?ls) in Pablo Larraín's [Spencer (2021)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt12536294/?ls). Moving deeper into the 2020s, she is working on [David Cronenberg](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000343/?ls)'s thriller [Crimes of the Future (2022)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt14549466/?ls).  
  
Stewart lives in Los Angeles, California.

Demi Lovato is a GRAMMY-nominated and award-winning musician, actor, advocate and New York Times best-selling author. She was first known for her onscreen talents, and soon after became a musical phenomenon for her remarkable vocal ability. With an audience of over 266 million on social media, Demi has established herself as a global sensation.  
  
With nearly 49 billion streams earned worldwide, Demi has captivated audiences with her renowned powerhouse vocals and illustrious songwriting. From the resilient ballad "Skyscraper," to the unapologetic earworm "Sorry Not Sorry" and her enduring queer anthem "Cool for the Summer," Demi's discography showcases her musicality knows no bounds, with a genre-blending approach that has infused pop, R&B, rock, soul and more. Through several sold-out tours, Demi has brought her undeniable stage presence to venues across the globe, while live performances such as her rendition of "The Star-Spangled Banner" at the Super Bowl LIV and the powerful debut of her single "Anyone" at the 62nd GRAMMY Awards have garnered universal acclaim.  
  
Demi has released eight studio albums, all of which debuted in the Top 10 of the Billboard 200 and four which boast over one billion streams on Spotify. Her most recent album, HOLY FVCK, is a sonic journey grounded in Demi's rock and pop-punk roots that illustrates an earnest yet tongue-in-cheek retrospective of her life experiences and opened to widespread acclaim from both critics and fans. The album was hailed as "the best we've heard from Lovato to date" (Variety) and was described as "fiery album filled with passion, thoughtful reflection, and a dash of good ol' fashioned rage" (Vogue), with Demi receiving praise as a vocal "powerhouse" (Pitchfork). HOLY FVCK debuted at #1 on several Billboard charts including the Top Rock & Alternative Albums chart, the Top Rock Albums chart, and the Top Alternative Albums chart. The album also marked Demi's eighth consecutive Top 10 album on the Billboard 200 and landed in the Top 5 of the Top Album Sales chart. The single "29" resonated with listeners worldwide and was deemed "the best song on the album" (TIME), with critics commending Demi's emotional delivery that reflects a "new, clear-eyed perspective" (Recording Academy).  
  
Most recently, Demi released her album REVAMPED featuring rock versions of her hit songs on September 15, 2023, which hit the top 10 of Billboard's Top New Albums Chart in line with Demi's previous releases. With all new vocals and production, the 10-track album REVAMPED sees Demi reimagine her career-defining songs with a fresh perspective that reflects her current artistic vision. The re-recorded music serves as another showcase of Demi's artistic growth and versatility, as she seamlessly evolves her songs from pop to rock while maintaining her signature powerhouse vocals.  
  
Demi has been lauded by fans and peers alike for her authenticity and vulnerability, demonstrating her transformative growth across two celebrated documentaries, 2017's Simply Complicated and 2021's Dancing with the Devil. As an advocate, Demi serves as Global Citizen's official ambassador for mental health, with a special focus on vulnerable communities around the world.  
  
Lovato has been honored with numerous awards and accolades over her career, including an MTV Video Music Award, 14 Teen Choice Awards, five People's Choice Awards, an ALMA Award, two Latin American Music Award and a GLAAD Vanguard Award for her services to LGBTQ+ activism. She has also received two GRAMMY Award nominations, four Billboard Music Awards nominations and three Brit Award nominations for her work.  
  
A native of Dallas, Demi resides in Los Angeles.

Lauren Keyana "Keke" Palmer was born on August 26, 1993, in Harvey, Illinois, and raised in Robbins, Illinois, to Sharon and Larry Palmer, both former actors. Palmer showed vocal promise as a five-year-old when she belted out "Jesus Loves Me" in her church choir. A year later, the singer-actress had a solo in her kindergarten play but, to her mom's dismay, the mic had not been adjusted to suit her daughter's height.  
  
Without missing a beat, Palmer lowered the mic and moved the crowd with her heavenly voice. At that very moment, her family knew there was something special about Keke (a nickname given to her by her sister).  
  
Although music was still her passion, Palmer's first big break came via her acting skills, making her big-screen debut in [Barbershop 2: Back in Business (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0337579/?ls) as [Queen Latifah](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001451/?ls)'s niece. Immediately recognizing her star potential, the film's producers encouraged her parents to take their daughter to California to explore other acting opportunities. Relocating required that Palmer's parents leave behind the security of their jobs, a newly purchased home, and uproot their other three children. However, it didn't diminish the family's support of Palmer's aspirations.  
  
Once settled on the West Coast, Palmer did not waste any time. Within six weeks she had booked an episode of the critically acclaimed CBS series [Cold Case (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0368479/?ls), a national K-Mart commercial, and was chosen from a nationwide search to play opposite [William H. Macy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000513/?ls) in a TNT movie, [The Wool Cap (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0377972/?ls). Her performance was so amazing that it earned her a Screen Actors Guild nomination - to date, she is the youngest actress (then at age 10) ever to receive a nomination in a Lead Actress Category.  
  
In 2006, Palmer appeared as the lead character "Akeelah Anderson" in the critically acclaimed, award-winning film [Akeelah and the Bee (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0437800/?ls). The film, about a young South Los Angeles girl who attempts to win a national spelling bee, won the hearts of audiences everywhere. Her breakthrough performance has received praise from many film critics and organizations. Among the list of nominations received, "Akeelah and the Bee" was listed as one of NBR's 2006 Top Independent Films of the Year, as well as four nominations from the NAACP Image Awards. Palmer, alone, won an NAACP Image Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Motion Picture, as well as Outstanding Lead Actress in a Motion Picture by the Black Movie Awards. She has also received nominations for Most Promising Newcomer by the Chicago Film Critics, Best Actress by the Black Reel Awards, and Best Young Actress by the Broadcast Film Critics Association. Keke held her own in scenes with veteran co-stars [Angela Bassett](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000291/?ls) and [Laurence Fishburne](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000401/?ls).  
  
That very same year, Palmer appeared in [Tyler Perry](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1347153/?ls)'s [Madea's Family Reunion (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0455612/?ls), which was #1 at the box office for two consecutive weeks. Palmer went on to win a 2007 NAACP Image Award for Outstanding Actress in a Motion Picture for her breakout role in "Akeelah and the Bee". (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0805559/?ls). This one-two punch of big-screen success coupled with small screen ratings power made Keke Palmer a household name in Hollywood.

This short film was created for every woman. The mother. The entrepreneur. The survivor. The perfectionist. The woman with anxiety. The woman carrying responsibilities no one knows about. The woman who looks in the mirror some mornings and has to remind herself who the hell she is. Because before the world sees the smile, the makeup, the outfit, the confidence, the mother, the partner, the professional, the creative…there is a woman standing alone with herself. And sometimes, before we can show up for everyone else, we have to speak life back into her. Before the World Sees Me started as a creative challenge. I wanted to take something as ordinary as getting ready and turn it into a story. What I didn’t expect was for the process of making it to mirror the message of the film itself. I have spent so much of my life waiting for the perfect moment. Waiting until I had the right tools. Waiting until an idea was polished enough. Waiting until I felt ready enough to allow people to see what I could create. So this time, I challenged myself to stop waiting. I wrote it. I directed it. I acted in it. I filmed it. I edited it. And I did it with the tool I already had in my hand…my iPhone. Is it perfect? Absolutely not. There are little things I already know I would shoot differently. Cuts I’d approach differently. Things I’ve learned about framing, continuity, pacing, sound and performance simply from making it. And I’m leaving some of those imperfections exactly where they are. Because this is my first short film. I don’t want to erase the beginning trying to make it look like I’ve already arrived. I want to be able to look back someday.. after film two, film ten, film twenty and see the woman who decided she didn’t need permission, perfect circumstances or perfect work to begin. Creating this taught me something I think I’m still learning in life: You don’t have to be finished to be worthy of being seen. So, this is me allowing myself to be seen. My very first short film: Before the World Sees Me. Written, directed, filmed, performed & edited by Jewell Moore. And I’m proud of her. #fyp Before the World Sees Me: A Woman's Journey. A short film celebrating the strength and resilience of every woman. Discover the journey of self-acceptance and creation, even with imperfections.

# Angeline Gragasin Talks Her Short Film Myself When I Am Real

 Angeline Gragasin. Contributed photo. 

by[![Image 3](https://filmobsessive.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/JPJ-1-400x404.jpg)**J Paul Johnson**](https://filmobsessive.com/author/j-paul-johnson/ [link_27] "Posts by J Paul Johnson")May 31, 2025, 12:00 am

Angeline Gragasin’s canny, touching short film _Myself When I Am Real_ presents itself as a circa-2000 home video unearthed from the vaults. But its MiniDV aesthetic, as simple as it is on the surface, is part of something far more complex. Gragasin’s is a film that in its short 18 minutes raises a set of probing questions about identity and assimilation, inviting its viewers to reflect on their own relationships and memories.

_Myself When I Am Real_ finds single mother Annette (Therese Dizon) and her shy teen daughter Jasmine (Lianah Sta. Ana) arriving at the home of a Filipino woman, Mercedes (Tina Chilip) and her friends for a Christmas party in the year 2000. Annette and Jasmine are not relatives of the host family; they’re barely acquaintances. But in their Eastern Wisconsin suburb, parties like Mercedes’ provide crucial connections for a community of people with a shared heritage. Of course, parties are also occasions for first impressions, as Annette fears and young Jasmine finds out—all too painfully.

Gragasin’s use of the era-appropriate MiniDV cams for the shoot lends a veneer of authenticity to _Myself When I Am Real_, the technique looking and feeling like observational documentary cinema. Yet to be clear, the film is a fiction, one that intentionally and artfully—even sometimes comically—blurs the lines between fiction and nonfiction.

Gragasin, raised herself in Wisconsin by her mother, who had immigrated as an adult from the Philippines, relies on both her own childhood memories and her adult reflections for the content of _Myself When I Am Real_. Her films have screened at BAM, Clermont-Ferrand, ZINEBI, Palais de Tokyo, Jumping Frames, and more. She teaches at Parsons School of Design in New York City. As _Myself When I Am Real_ continues its international festival run, she spoke to Film Obsessive publisher [J Paul Johnson](link_27) about the film’s inception, production, and reception.

The transcript following the video below has been edited for space and clarity.

[Video 1](link_28)

**Film Obsessive: I’m excited to talk about your film. You’ve been very busy, it sounds like, on the festival circuit. Where has the film been and what kind of reception have you garnered?**

**Angeline Gragasin:** Yeah, we’ve had an amazing festival run so far. I just got back from [CAAMfest Center for Asian American Media Festival in San Francisco](link_29), preparing to play at the [Palm Springs International Short Film Festival](link_30) next month. And at some of my favorite festivals, I’ve noticed the film has been programmed alongside hybrid films. We played at the [New/Next Film Festival](link_31) last fall. This was actually my favorite. My film is a longer short, and they programmed us beside a shorter feature (_A Man Imagined_) by a filmmaking duo called Cassidy and Shatzki and theirs was a hybrid doc film—a documentary film that had some fictional elements. And my film, as you know, is a fictional film that has documentary elements, or you could call it an autofictional film.

It was really amazing to be in dialogue with just one film to allow the audience to focus more on my film in relation to this other film. [Women Make Waves International Film Festival in Taipei](link_32) also programmed me in this way. I think that’s a really exciting way to present the work in terms of its formal qualities. I mean, I must admit, I feel like pigeonholing it as a coming of age film or like an Asian film or a Filipino film has been somewhat frustrating for me because the hope is that it’s so much more than that. But I’ve had a great time so far and the shorts block we’re playing in Palm Springs is called “Life of the Party.” They haven’t announced the lineup yet, but I imagine the film will be played alongside other short films having to do with parties, which also I find very intriguing, and I’m excited to see that program.

**That sounds fascinating. You say you might not wish for the film to be pigeonholed as, say, a coming of age film or an Asian film, et cetera. Yet It is those things, and it is far more than those things. You also describe it as an autofiction, which is an interesting term. Can I have you, for our audience, in the most efficient way you can, describe what the film is and does?**

Yes. Well, autofiction, I mean, that term has only recently found its way into the cinematic discourse, and it comes from literary criticism, an autobiographical work with fictional elements or that is somewhat fictionalized. So, in many ways, my film is based on my own lived experience, and therefore is autobiographical to some extent, but also very, very heavily fictionalized. But the film is about a mother and daughter who attend a Christmas party in suburban Wisconsin. It’s a Filipino Christmas party specifically, and it’s shot on MiniDV in the style of a home movie. So, the idea is we’re getting this slice of life glimpse into this dysfunctional Filipino Christmas party, shifting perspective between the mother and child.

![Image 4: Jasmine (Lianah Sta. Ana) sings during the party.](https://filmobsessive.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Still-2-4-700x449.png)

Lianah Sta. Ana as Jasmine, the daughter, in _Myself When I Am Real_. Photo: Weird Seed Productions.

**It’s really charming and it’s really funny. I had a couple of really good laughs at it and it’s also a very insightful treatment of the relationship between mother and daughter as they’re in a new place. It’s set in suburban Wisconsin. Is that where you’re from?**

Yes. I grew up in Racine, Wisconsin, which is just south of Milwaukee. It’s almost on the border of Wisconsin and Illinois on Lake Michigan.

**And can I ask to what extent the film is or is not autobiographical?**

That’s a very good question. To what extent? Well, I am Filipino American, I mean, American born to a Filipino immigrant single mother, as are the characters in the film. I grew up going to parties like the one depicted in the film. Um, now, the occupation of the mother, that’s where the similarities end and details, I think that were written into the film for character development, just for the purposes of storytelling, there are some embellishments there. But I guess the quality of the relationship and the environment that you’re seeing, that is very much rooted in my own lived experience and true to life, I would say.

![Image 5: Therese Dizon as Annette](https://filmobsessive.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Still-3-1-700x441.png)

Therese Dizon as Annette, the mother, , the daughter, in _Myself When I Am Real._ Photo: Weird Seed Productions.

**Okay. The entire film is set in one single party over the course of what, perhaps a few hours?**

Yes. So you get to see, you know, a little bit during the day and then sunsets and you see, you know, it continues on into the night. And it’s a period piece that takes place in the year 2000. So all very accurate.

**And did that setting have something to do with why you went to the MiniDV home media style of shooting?**

Yes. So when I had written this, I wasn’t sure what camera I wanted to shoot it on. I didn’t quite have the visual style fully developed. Until at some point, I thought, I think I’d like for this to look and feel like a home movie, like an authentic archival home movie that was unearthed, a tape that you found that hadn’t been played since 2000. I brought this to my DP, Yujin Yohe, and he said, “Oh, that’s a great idea, but in the year 2000 people weren’t shooting on VHS anymore, people were shooting on MiniDV. Would you consider that?” I was like, “Oh, yeah, you’re right. Of course.”

Rather than shooting on a consumer level camera for maximum authenticity—because we know this is a fictional film that’s going to have a theatrical release—we wanted to increase the production value. He proposed shooting on the same camera that Thomas Vinterberg shot [_Festen_ _(_ aka _A Celebration)_](link_33) on. That camera is the Canon Excel II. So we shot on MiniDV as per Yujin’s suggestion, which I really, really loved, and we did not the one thing we did not do that Thomas Vinterberg does, is transpose that to 35mm film. It’s just the raw tape, what you’re seeing purely out of the camera with no visual effects, no color correction. So all of those glitches and artifacts or happened organically in camera. But I see that as a happy accident and it gives texture and grain and adds to the film’s archival quality and the authenticity of feeling like, “Okay, this is a real home movie tape with all of its imperfections.”

**Is it a one-camera shoot, then?**

Yes.

**Let me focus on editing that footage because you’re doing a lot of work here to do things that a director not shooting in this style would not do. You would not have the camera person be present in the diegesis of the film and told to get out of the way. Can you talk a little bit about how mindful you are of this visual design when you are both shooting and editing the project?**

That’s a really great question, and I’m so glad you asked about it. Yes, I was very intentional with choreographing. Well, it wasn’t totally choreographed. There’s a lot of improvisation and spontaneity from the performers. But, Yujin and I made a decision, my DP and I, that the perspective of the camera person is a character in the film—in the diegesis of the film, as you say. We decided not to name this person because it wasn’t relevant to the story, you know, who is behind the camera. We wanted to just look and feel like they were another guest at the party, which is what allowed you to have that level of access and intimacy, seeing things, private moments, that a professional camera person might not have access to.

And, we did a lot of rehearsals with the actors where we’re trying to not only capture the action for storytelling so that you can understand what a character’s motivations are or see their reaction at a certain moment, et cetera. But we also did a lot of work to mimic the quality of amateur videography or of a home movie cameraperson. Meaning, at some point I realized after we rehearsed enough times, Yujin had started to anticipate the actions because they’re scripted. And a lot of my direction on set was, “Don’t anticipate. You don’t know what’s going to happen next, so there needs to be a delay.” When you’re moving the camera, if action happens over here, over there, you know, you can’t follow the action. There always needs to be a delayed reaction, and it just needs to feel more spontaneous and organic. A lot of the choreography Yujin and I were doing were one, following the action for storytelling purposes, and then two, inhabiting the perspective of the camera person as a character, discovering moments for the first time and following it as like a documentary cinematographer, would without knowing in advance.

![Image 6: (l-R) DP Yujin Yeho, director Angeline Gragasin (behin the camera) and actor Tina Chilip on the set of Myself When I Am Real"](https://filmobsessive.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Myself-when-I-am-Real-700x493.jpg)

(l-R) DP Yujin Yohe, director Angeline Gragasin (behin the camera) and actor Tina Chilip on the set of _Myself When I Am Real_. Contributed photo.

**It leads to some marvelous moments in the film with some action taking place outside what the normal perspective of the party would be. We look for instance, at a conversation on a couch between two people who are dancing, we do a little bit of eavesdropping there. We go under the table for one important detail, and then at the end, there’s a climactic moment that happens offscreen doing just exactly what you described, the camera has to follow and catch up with a sound that’s important. All of that is really cool.**

**Was Vinterberg a model for you or were there other films or filmmakers that you look to in thinking this through?**

Well, Vinterberg was Yujin’s reference. I had actually never seen the film before he brought it up, and I think he brought it up because it’s also about a party that goes wrong, and that takes place all in one location. And so, we watched that as a reference for this film.

But, zooming out in general, I’m very much attracted to fiction films that feel like documentary and documentaries that feel like fiction. So films that just blur the line between fiction and nonfiction, I would say my greatest influence and biggest inspiration is Agnes Varda. She made her whole career of moving between fiction and nonfiction—before we had this thing called hybrid film. She was already experimenting with that. And she was one of the first filmmakers to adopt MiniDV, also, I think, about 2000, so she’s a huge inspiration to me, and I [was fortunate enough to be able to interview her in 2017](link_34), which was a meaningful and life-changing, transformative experience, [given] her approach to perspective and the conflict between reality and artifice, private and public.

[![Image 7: Agnes Varda being interviewed in 2017.](https://filmobsessive.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/VS-THEELEMENTSOFAGNES2017onVimeo-019-700x394.jpg)](https://vimeo.com/327297102 [link_34])

Agnes Varda, being interviewed by filmmaker Angeline Gragasin in 2017.

All of that has influenced me as a storyteller. I’m very drawn to films that are about public and private self image or our relationship to our own image. Those are themes that are present in her work, and also structurally, how she tells the story is she’s very rigorous in the screenwriting. That’s a huge influence to me as well.

**And so, that’s an interesting journey. You were a suburban Wisconsin kid some 25 years ago, now making your way as an accomplished filmmaker through the festival circuit. What’s your journey been like?**

Well, I fell into filmmaking by accident. I loved movies growing up, but it never occurred to me that I myself could make movies, could become a filmmaker. I didn’t know anyone who was a filmmaker, and I’m a millennial. I came of age during the digital revolution. So we were still shooting on MiniDV and films with theatrical release were still all shot on 35, and it just seemed like this faraway foreign alien world impenetrable and very exclusive and inaccessible to someone like me. But I had a really amazing education in Wisconsin. I went to a really small K-12 school. I went there through age seven to 17, and it had a huge influence on me because I had a really incredible fine and performing arts program. I was exposed to a lot of different media and a lot of different international artists and traditions, not only in the visual arts, but in music and theater. So, I studied a lot of different ways of making as a child. And then, I ended up going to the University of Chicago for my undergraduate degree, where I majored in interdisciplinary studies in the humanities.

**Was that with an eye towards filmmaking or was that art form that you came at still later?**

It was much later. So at Chicago, my concentration was theater and performance studies. And I focused on avant-garde Polish theater making, experimental theater. I was studying [Jerzy] Grotowski, I was studying Tadeusz Kantor and then I was also studying Commedia dell’arte and studying training with theater artists who had trained at Jacques Lecoq. So that was really my focus as a performer, but also as a writer and a director. It’s a very interdisciplinary craft. That’s the foundation, I would say, for my practice as a filmmaker.

And then I just randomly fell into it. I was cast in an Indie feature by an emerging filmmaker in Chicago. And I had so much fun, but I thought, “Oh, I really want to be on the other side of the camera. That seems much more interesting to me.”And my favorite part about filmmaking is collaboration. Just it’s essential. It’s necessary. You must collaborate to make a film. And so that

# How Facebook uses the email or mobile phone number on your profile

Copy link

 We’re gradually updating people to [Meta Accounts](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.meta.com%2Fhelp%2Fmeta-account%2F876751767182450%3Fhelpref%3Dfaq_content&h=AUDOjiWmHVLPnYxIZpUvnT2cRjIfgco_PqV2hEZxACMaXW7YvlKtNuJ6TGQG4gUZfVV5NFl-fAo61RrG8G9cMn33nZbZOalILH57MIABUqB5ysLqCjUxiwsp39TwAk5_wQ5AJpSHpMMVYA). You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

## How we use your email address or mobile phone number

We may use your email address or mobile phone number for purposes like:

*   [Helping you log in](https://www.facebook.com/help/283100488694834?helpref=faq_content). If you forget your password, you'll need an updated phone number or email address to reset it. If you forget or [lose access](https://www.facebook.com/help/132243923516844?helpref=faq_content) to the email address or phone number associated with your account, you can use one to look up the other. 
*   Sending you email, WhatsApp and SMS notifications for updates about activity on your account, promotions and account safety. These notifications can help keep your account safe through features like two-factor authentication and alerts about unrecognized logins.
*   Providing and improving ads for you and others. We use your contact information alongside information we get from your activity to help us improve our ads services for everyone within the Facebook community.
*   Some of our security checkpoints can be difficult to pass using assistive technology. If you add a mobile number or email address to your Facebook account, you'll have another way to verify your account if you need to pass any of these checkpoints. Keep in mind that these checkpoints may require internet access. 

By entering your phone number, you authorize your mobile network provider to share data from your account and device to Facebook or its service providers for phone number verification and fraud prevention purposes. Learn more about the data we collect and how we use it in our [Privacy Policy](https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/).

We never sell personal information, including your email address and phone number, to anyone. Keep in mind that you can control who can [see your contact information](https://www.facebook.com/help/117118145038822?helpref=faq_content) and who we can [suggest your profile to](https://www.facebook.com/help/131297846947406?helpref=faq_content) based on your phone number or email address. Learn more about how Facebook uses your phone number and email address in our [Privacy Policy.](https://www.facebook.com/about/privacy)

You may see an email or phone number suggested for you when we ask you to add your contact information. Emails or phone numbers shown in this way will only be added to your account if you choose to [add them](https://www.facebook.com/help/223900927622502?helpref=faq_content).

## How we suggest email addresses or phone numbers

We may suggest an email address or phone number for you based on information we receive from sources such as: 

*   Contact information provided by others on Facebook.
*   An email address or phone number that you entered previously but didn't confirm.
*   Your mobile phone or tablet.

## Reasons for confirming your mobile phone number

We may ask you to confirm your mobile phone number because:

*   You previously [added the phone number](https://www.facebook.com/help/297947214257999?helpref=faq_content) we're asking you to confirm.
*   Time has passed since you last added or updated your phone number.
*   We’ve received information from your device that helps us suggest the number connected to that device.
*   You haven’t added one yet, and we want to show you how.

## More information

*   [Add or remove a mobile phone number.](https://www.facebook.com/help/124895950923762?helpref=faq_content)
*   [Add or remove an email address.](https://www.facebook.com/help/162801153783275?helpref=faq_content)
*   [Adjust how you get notifications.](https://www.facebook.com/help/390022341057202?helpref=faq_content)

# Complete Film Winners From the 31st Critics Choice Awards

 Chelsea Handler at the 31st Annual Critics Choice Awards Photo by Kevin Winter/Getty Images for the CCA. 

by[![Image 3](https://filmobsessive.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/DSC_0077-e1786338050147-400x401.jpg)**Don Shanahan**](https://filmobsessive.com/author/everymoviehasalesson/ "Posts by Don Shanahan")9 months ago

This past Sunday, the Critics Choice Association ([CCA](https://www.criticschoice.com/)) announced the winners of the 31st annual Critics Choice Awards. The star-studded awards ceremony, hosted by Chelsea Handler, was held once again at the Barker Hangar in Santa Monica and aired live on both coasts on E! and USA Network. The show is now available to stream on Peacock. Film Obsessive Editor in Chief [Don Shanahan](https://filmobsessive.com/author/everymoviehasalesson/) is a proud voting member of the Critics Choice Association.

![Image 4: Several people gather on stage while a man accepts an award at the 31st Critics Choice Awards.](https://filmobsessive.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/2254688333-700x501.jpg)

[Share](https://filmobsessive.com/film/film-news/film-awards/complete-film-winners-from-the-31st-critics-choice-awards/#)

[Share on Pinterest](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button?url=https://filmobsessive.com/film/film-news/film-awards/complete-film-winners-from-the-31st-critics-choice-awards/&description=Complete%20Film%20Winners%20From%20the%2031st%20Critics%20Choice%20Awards&media=https%3A%2F%2Ffilmobsessive.com%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2026%2F01%2F2254688333-700x501.jpg "Share on Pinterest")[Share on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?app_id=&display=popup&href=https://filmobsessive.com/film/film-news/film-awards/complete-film-winners-from-the-31st-critics-choice-awards/&quote=Complete%20Film%20Winners%20From%20the%2031st%20Critics%20Choice%20Awards "Share on Facebook")[Share on Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https://filmobsessive.com/film/film-news/film-awards/complete-film-winners-from-the-31st-critics-choice-awards/&text=Complete%20Film%20Winners%20From%20the%2031st%20Critics%20Choice%20Awards%20 "Share on Twitter")

(L-R) Benicio del Toro, Leonardo DiCaprio, Cassandra Kulukundis, Paul Thomas Anderson and Chase Infiniti at the 31st Critics Choice Awards. Photo by Kevin Winter/Getty Images for the CCA.

_One Battle After Another_ won Best Picture. In addition to Best Picture, the lightning rod film starring the nominated Leonardo DiCaprio took home trophies for both Best Director and Best Adapted Screenplay, both going to celebrated filmmaker Paul Thomas Anderson.

Meanwhile _Frankenstein_ and _Sinners_ garnered the most wins in the film categories, with both films taking home four trophies each. _Frankenstein_ won Best Supporting Actor for Jacob Elordi, Best Production Design for Tamara Deverell and Shane Vieau, Best Costume Design for Kate Hawley, and Best Hair and Makeup for Mike Hill, Jordan Samuel and Cliona Furey. _Sinners_ won Best Young Actor/Actress for Miles Caton, Best Original Screenplay for Ryan Coogler, Best Casting and Ensemble for Francine Maisler, and Best Score for Ludwig Göransson.

The Critics Choice Awards are bestowed annually to honor the finest in cinematic and television achievement. Historically, they are the most accurate predictor of Academy Award nominations. The 31st annual Critics Choice Awards show was executive-produced by Bob Bain Productions and Berlin Entertainment. The Critics Choice Awards are represented by Dan Black at Greenberg Traurig, LLP. Sponsors of the Awards included FIJI Water, Milagro Tequila, Cold Stone Creamery, and Wetzel’s Pretzels.

Leading into the show, the “LIVE from E!: Critics Choice Awards” red carpet special aired live from 2:00-4:00 p.m. PT / 5:00-7:00 p.m. ET across E!, USA Network and Peacock. The special was hosted by Justin Sylvester and Keltie Knight, along with Will Marfuggi and Erin Lim.

_**COMPLETE WINNERS OF THE FILM CATEGORIES FROM THE 31ST ANNUAL CRITICS CHOICE AWARDS:**_

**BEST PICTURE**  
_One Battle After Another_

**BEST ACTOR**  
 Timothée Chalamet – _Marty Supreme_

**BEST ACTRESS**  
 Jessie Buckley – _Hamnet_

**BEST SUPPORTING ACTOR**  
 Jacob Elordi – _Frankenstein_

**BEST SUPPORTING ACTRESS**  
 Amy Madigan – _Weapons_

**BEST YOUNG ACTOR / ACTRESS**  
 Miles Caton – _Sinners_

**BEST DIRECTOR**  
 Paul Thomas Anderson – _One Battle After Another_

**BEST ORIGINAL SCREENPLAY**  
 Ryan Coogler – _Sinners_

**BEST ADAPTED SCREENPLAY**  
 Paul Thomas Anderson – _One Battle After Another_

**BEST CASTING AND ENSEMBLE**  
 Francine Maisler – _Sinners_

**BEST CINEMATOGRAPHY**|  
 Adolpho Veloso – _Train Dreams_

**BEST PRODUCTION DESIGN**  
 Tamara Deverell, Shane Vieau – _Frankenstein_

**BEST EDITING**  
 Stephen Mirrione – _F1_

**BEST COSTUME DESIGN**  
 Kate Hawley – _Frankenstein_

**BEST HAIR AND MAKEUP**  
 Mike Hill, Jordan Samuel, Cliona Furey – _Frankenstein_

**BEST VISUAL EFFECTS**  
 Joe Letteri, Richard Baneham, Eric Saindon, Daniel Barrett – _Avatar: Fire and Ash_

**BEST STUNT DESIGN**  
 Wade Eastwood – _Mission: Impossible – The Final Reckoning_

**BEST ANIMATED FEATURE**  
_KPop Demon Hunters_

**BEST COMEDY**  
_The Naked Gun_

**BEST FOREIGN LANGUAGE FILM**  
_The Secret Agent_

**BEST SONG**  
 “Golden” – Ejae, Mark Sonnenblick, Ido, 24, Teddy – _KPop Demon Hunters_

**BEST SCORE**  
 Ludwig Göransson – _Sinners_

**BEST SOUND**  
 Al Nelson, Gwendolyn Yates Whittle, Gary A. Rizzo, Juan Peralta, Gareth John – _F1_

_**About the Critics Choice Association (CCA)**_

The Critics Choice Association is the largest critics organization in the United States and Canada, representing more than 500 media critics and entertainment journalists. It was established in 2019 with the formal merger of the Broadcast Film Critics Association and the Broadcast Television Journalists Association, recognizing the intersection between film, television, and streaming content. For more information, visit: [www.CriticsChoice.com](https://slate-pr.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=28481e1d13b3d43b2cb793280&id=84ac477f5c&e=077d277a8b).

Follow the 31st annual Critics Choice Awards on Instagram and X @CriticsChoice, on TikTok @OfficialCriticsChoice, and on Facebook/CriticsChoiceAwards. Join the conversation using #CriticsChoiceAwards. Follow @enews and @eentertainment for red carpet and CCA coverage.
